hep-ex.title: Deep-learning-based low-energy trigger algorithms for the Hyper-Kamiokande experiment
hep-ex.author: Katharina Lachner, Saúl Alonso-Monsalve, Benjamin Richards, Davide Sgalaberna
hep-ex.abstract: Modern machine learning techniques have become increasingly important in particle physics because of their powerful pattern-recognition capabilities, including in real-time data acquisition where stringent runtime constraints apply. This paper details the performance of deep-learning-based trigger algorithms for a large water Cherenkov detector such as Hyper-Kamiokande, aimed at low-energy neutrino events (below 7 MeV). The performance of custom neural-network supervised classifiers is shown alongside two anomaly-detection approaches trained solely on detector noise: a pure autoencoder and a model based on Manifold Projection-Diffusion Recovery. The supervised model shows signal identification efficiencies of 76.7% for single electrons of 3 MeV kinetic energy, significantly exceeding signal efficiencies obtained from a traditional hit-count-based trigger of 26.4%, while the Manifold Projection-Diffusion Recovery approach reaches 35.4% at the same operating point. Runtime evaluations on GPU yield per-window inference latencies well below the millisecond scale.

hep-ex.title: First measurement of flux of the neutron background induced by accelerated neutrinos at the J-PARC facility
hep-ex.author: Hiroshi Ito, Ryo Shibayama, Chisako Ise, Akihiro Minamino, Yusuke Koshio, Masaki Ishitsuka

hep-ex.title: Single inclusive hadron and jet production in lepton-hadron scattering
hep-ex.author: Jian-Wei Qiu, Kazuhiro Watanabe
hep-ex.abstract: We present the first calculation of single inclusive hadron and jet production at large transverse momentum in lepton-hadron scattering in a joint QCD+QED factorization approach. The scattering cross section is factorized into a convolution of infrared-safe hard coefficient functions with universal lepton distribution functions (LDFs) and parton distribution functions (PDFs) of the colliding lepton and hadron, respectively, together with fragmentation functions (FFs) of the observed hadron (or jet). With joint QCD+QED factorization, the Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) type evolution equations for LDFs, PDFs, and FFs necessarily have evolution kernels calculated in both QCD and QED. We derive a default set of LDFs for our calculations and discuss a strategy to extract universal, non-perturbative LDFs from future data. We present our calculations for single inclusive hadron and/or jet production at the energies of Jefferson Lab and the future Electron-Ion Collider.

hep-ex.title: Optical Characterization Measurements of Commercial Polyvinyltoluene Scintillators for Accurate Geant4 Detector Modeling
hep-ex.author: Fergus Martin Huggins, Micah S. Johnson, Matthew Quinn Buckner
hep-ex.abstract: Accurate Monte Carlo simulation of plastic scintillator detectors requires precise wavelength-dependent optical properties. We present measurements of wavelength-dependent refractive index $n(\lambda)$ and bulk absorption length $L_{\mathrm{abs}}(\lambda)$ for six commercial polyvinyltoluene (PVT)-based scintillators (Saint Gobain BC-400, BC-404, BC-408, BC-418, BC-422, and BC-430) at five wavelengths between 372 and 660 nm. Using a precision refraction apparatus and variable-thickness transmission measurements, we characterize material-specific dispersion that deviates substantially from both the manufacturer specification and literature values for pure PVT. Illustrative Geant4 simulations of a BC-422 detector demonstrate a 7.2% reduction in photocathode energy-deposition threshold events when using our measured $n(\lambda)$ compared to the constant manufacturer value, highlighting the practical importance of accurate optical property data for detector design and calibration. We successfully measure absorption lengths for BC-430 at four wavelengths between 372 and 505 nm (2.2-12.4 mm) and for all materials at 372 nm (2.2-38 mm), while establishing lower bounds exceeding 750 mm for weakly absorbing formulations at longer wavelengths.

hep-ex.title: Reassessing the $X(2370)$ in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$ beyond the one-dimensional mass projections
hep-ex.author: Xiang-Kun Dong, Teng Ji, Meike Küßner, Ulf-G. Meißner
hep-ex.abstract: The BESIII Collaboration recently extracted the properties of the $X(2370)$ from a fit to the one-dimensional $K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$ invariant-mass spectrum in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$. The intermediate two-body structures visible in the mass correlations, including the $K_0^*(1430)$ bands, require a coherent treatment of cross-channel interference when interpreting the enhancement near 2.3 GeV. We reassess the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution by fitting the published data using an effective coupled-channel framework with an approximate detection efficiency depending on the three-body invariant mass. The three-body parent amplitude is parameterized using a $K$-matrix that describes scattering among several quasi-two-body channels. The seven- and eight-bare-state models give similar mass distributions. Adding the eighth bare state lowers the Poisson deviance by 1.22% and produces an additional pole at $E=(2419-i152)$ MeV, substantially broader than the $X(2370)$ mass-width reference. This pole is model-dependent, and its identification with the $X(2370)$ is not clear. The present analysis does not establish the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$, thereby weakening the flavor-singlet argument based on the suppression of $K^*\bar K$ relative to the total $K\bar K\pi$ contribution. A more comprehensive experimental amplitude analysis, incorporating coherent interference, mass and angular correlations, and detector effects across related decay channels, is needed to establish the role and decay properties of the $X(2370)$.

hep-ph.title: Causal-horizon scaling of prompt X(3872) formation lengths
hep-ph.author: Yi Yang
hep-ph.abstract: We use conventional charmonium as a spatial ruler for the correlations accessed in prompt X(3872) formation. In a Gaussian source model, averaging an early phase field over an exponential causal-horizon ensemble gives a leading formation loss linear in the sampled length. Comparing the changes of two adjacent production ratios removes the common field strength, horizon scale and exposure. Potential-model charmonium separation lengths then calibrate the remaining length gaps. Matched LHCb measurements at 13 TeV give, for a common source and a direct J/psi reference, a central lower X(3872) formation profile scale of about 1.3 fm and a central lower prepared source scale of about 0.65 fm. An arbitrarily compact common source cannot reproduce the observed difference simply by increasing the final profile. These formation constraints permit an arbitrarily long final-state tail. A fixed proper-exposure rule is separately tested against conventional-charmonium activity data and prompt X(3872)/psi(2S) jet shapes. Prompt feed-down and relative production changes quantify the sensitivity of the extraction. A matched activity measurement of all three states tests the inferred spatial ordering.

hep-ph.title: Explaining $b\to s\ell^+\ell^-$ with CKM Unitarity Violation? A No-Go Theorem
hep-ph.author: Andreas Crivellin, Matthew Kirk
hep-ph.abstract: The deficits w.r.t.~the Standard Model predictions in $B\to K^{(*)}\mu^+\mu^-$ and $B_s\to \phi\mu^+\mu^-$ have recently been substantiated by new analyses from LHCb and CMS, as well as improved theoretical predictions, resulting in strong statistical evidence for lepton flavour universal new physics effects. In this letter, we investigate the possibility of generating such an effect through CKM unitarity violation: If the true value of $V_{cb}$, extracted from $B\to D^{(*)}\ell\nu$, were larger due to an NP contamination, this would lead, via the assumed CKM unitarity within the SM, to a smaller value of $V_{ts}$ and thus to reduced theory predictions for $b\to s\ell^+\ell^-$ branching ratios. A sizable correction to the $W$-$c$-$b$ vertex is only possible close to the custodial-protected limit in which $Z$-$b$-$s$ couplings are absent. However, in a model-independent SMEFT analysis, we show that even if $C_{Hq}^{(1)}=-C_{Hq}^{(3)}$ is realized at a high scale, additional custodial-breaking effects appear due to RGE. Therefore, only a fine-tuned region in the parameter space of modified gauge boson couplings, displaying an overcompensation of the CKM unitarity-violating effect, gives a good fit to $b\to s\ell^+\ell^-$ data. The only realistic simple SM extensions to achieve this setup are vector-like quarks. However, we show that they cannot explain the $b\to s\ell^+\ell^-$ anomalies without violating bounds for electroweak precision observables as well as $K^0-\bar K^0$ and $B_s-\bar B_s$ mixing.

hep-ph.title: Entropy Production and Thermalization in Heavy-Quark Langevin Dynamics
hep-ph.author: A. M. Silva
hep-ph.abstract: Heavy quarks are often treated as Brownian probes of the quark-gluon plasma. We formulate the irreversible entropy balance of their momentum distribution and separate the production generated by collisions from the driving caused by an evolving medium. For linear dynamics the production splits into two positive contributions, from directed momentum and from the momentum width. A static bath obeys an exact H-theorem. A cooling bath adds an explicit driving term, and longitudinal Bjorken expansion enters as a separate kinematic drive rather than as collisional production. For a Bjorken temperature protocol we derive closed-form strong- and weak-coupling limits of the total production. At strong coupling it exceeds the initial relative entropy by a term linear in the relaxation time, whose quasistatic part has the thermodynamic-length form. At weak coupling it vanishes inversely with the relaxation time. A positive strong-coupling slope therefore guarantees maximal dissipation at intermediate coupling. The same structure holds for a relativistic Fokker-Planck equation with a Jüttner stationary state, solved numerically for charm and bottom quarks under the temperature protocol. Linear-response coefficients computed from the static generator reproduce both limits, and the numerical entropy balance is satisfied to high accuracy.

hep-ph.title: Constraints on Decaying Dark Matter with $B=1$ from Fermi-LAT
hep-ph.author: Can Kilic, Zhi-Xiang Yang, Taewook Youn
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the gamma ray signatures of fermionic dark matter that carries one unit of baryon number and decays into three quarks. We compute the expected prompt and secondary gamma-ray spectra for a representative range of final state flavor combinations. By comparing these spectra to Fermi-LAT measurements of the isotropic gamma-ray background, we derive exclusion limits on the lifetime. We observe that depending on the dark matter mass and the flavor of the final state, the lifetime bounds on decays of $B=1$ dark matter can differ by up to a factor of two from those on decays of $B=0$ dark matter. Furthermore, light-quark final states generally yield stronger bounds at lower masses, whereas heavy-quark final states can yield comparable or stronger bounds at masses of tens of TeV and above.

hep-ph.title: The Singular Structure of Rapidity Distributions for Color-Singlet Production at N3LO
hep-ph.author: Federica Devoto, Bernhard Mistlberger, Gherardo Vita
hep-ph.abstract: We determine the universal singular structure of rapidity distributions for color-singlet production in hadron collisions through next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N3LO) in QCD. Our result captures the full singular contributions as either partonic momentum fraction approaches one, including the delta-function terms, while retaining the exact dependence on the other. The essential new ingredient is the complete calculation of the three-loop quark and gluon rapidity beam-function matching kernels. Our calculation is based on the strict collinear expansion of the partonic cross sections for Higgs boson and Drell-Yan production. We represent our results in terms of generalized polylogarithms as well as numerical series expansions. The resulting N3LO partonic coefficient functions apply to arbitrary color-singlet production processes with the process dependence entering through the hard function, which encodes the virtual corrections to the Born process.

hep-ph.title: Gauge Interactions Involving New Vector and Pseudoscalar Particles
hep-ph.author: Ruiyu Xing, Honglei Li, Zhi-Long Han, Fei Huang, Cui-Juan Lv, Xinyi Zhang
hep-ph.abstract: The Vector gauge bosons $Z'$ and axion-like particles (ALPs) $a$ are predicted by the $U(1)_X$ gauge extension and Peccei-Quinn (PQ) models, respectively. We focus on the interactions of the $Z'$ boson and the $a$ particle with the $W^\pm$ gauge boson, and investigate the production cross section and related kinematic distributions for the $Z'/a\to W^+W^-$ decay process at hadron colliders. We consider the angular distributions of charged leptons in the final states corresponding to the semileptonic and fully leptonic decays of the $W^\pm$ boson, separately. The study shows that, in the associated production processes of $Z'/a$ with $W^+$ or $Z$ bosons, the angular distributions of final-state leptons can serve as an important observable for probing new gauge interactions, and can also provide a criterion to distinguish vector particles from pseudoscalar particles.

hep-ph.title: About All-Charm Tetraquarks in S and P Waves
hep-ph.author: Hugo Garcia Tecocoatzi, Luciano Maiani, Elena Santopinto, Veronica Riquer, Ailer Rivero-Acosta
hep-ph.abstract: We present a quantitative analysis of masses and decays of $cc \bar c \bar c$ tetraquarks, with diquarks and antidiquarks in S and P wave. We study explicitely the decays of the $4P-J^{PC}=3^{--},~2^{--}$ into 4 muons and into hidden- and open-charm mesons and estimate its width and branching ratios. Based on our results and with the present sensitivity, LHCb, CMS and ATLAS should detect the $4P-J^{PC}=3^{--},~2^{--}$ fully-charmed tetraquark. We note that one decay channel of the $4P-J^{PC}=2^{--}$could lead to the identification of the (still controversial) $\chi_{c1}(2P)$.

hep-ph.title: Search for dark photon in association with charged leptons at electron-positron colliders
hep-ph.author: Dai-Xing Zhang, Chang-Qi Hu, Chun-Yuan Li, Xiao Liang, Xing-Hua Yang
hep-ph.abstract: The dark photon can serve as a vector portal between the dark sector and the Standard Model via kinetic mixing. In this paper, we investigate the production of an invisible dark photon via the process $e^+ e^- \to \ell^+ \ell^- A'$ with $\ell=e,\mu$, at the Circular Electron Positron Collider (CEPC). The production cross sections for the signal process are calculated, and the kinematic distributions for the signal and background processes are analyzed. We further compute the branching ratio for the invisible decay of the dark photon, and explore the discovery potential of dark photons at the CEPC. It is found that dark photons with masses in the range $1~\mathrm{GeV} < M_{A'} < 16~\mathrm{GeV}$ are potentially detectable at the CEPC.

hep-ph.title: Leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude from scalar and axial-vector diquark correlations
hep-ph.author: B. Almeida-Zamora, L. Albino, C. Mezrag, J. Segovia
hep-ph.abstract: We compute the leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude (PDA) using algebraic representations of the nucleon Faddeev wave function inspired by perturbation-theory integral representations. The PDA is obtained from a light-front projection of the covariant quark--diquark Faddeev amplitude and analysed in terms of its scalar- and axial-vector-diquark components. We derive analytic expressions for the corresponding diquark distribution amplitudes and their contributions to the proton PDA. The resulting distribution is broad and concave, with its maximum $(x_1,x_2,x_3)\approx(0.55,0.20,0.25)$ displaced from the symmetric configuration $(1/3,1/3,1/3)$, which corresponds to the maximum of the perturbative-QCD asymptotic form. Scalar-diquark correlations generate a strong asymmetry in the longitudinal momentum distribution, whereas axial-vector correlations redistribute momentum among the valence quarks and significantly reduce this asymmetry. We calculate low-order Mellin moments and obtain a compact parametrisation of the proton PDA at the hadronic scale, $\mu_0=0.51\,\mathrm{GeV}$. We then perform the leading-order QCD evolution of its normalized shape to $\mu=2\,\mathrm{GeV}$, finding that evolution reduces the momentum asymmetry while preserving a clear imprint of the non-perturbative quark--diquark correlations. The results provide insight into the role of such correlations in shaping the proton light-front structure and furnish non-perturbative input for studies of hard exclusive baryonic processes.

hep-ph.title: Anisotropic hadronic matter in external magnetic fields
hep-ph.author: Dushmanta Sahu, Jayanta Dey
hep-ph.abstract: Strong magnetic fields generated in non-central heavy-ion collisions break rotational symmetry and can imprint anisotropy on the produced quantum chromodynamics (QCD) matter. Within a hadron resonance gas framework in the presence of an external magnetic field, we investigate the resulting anisotropy in the equation of state, isothermal compressibility, speed of sound, and conserved-charge fluctuations. We find that the electric-charge susceptibility ratio $\chi_4^Q/\chi_2^Q$ develops a pronounced directional dependence, driven primarily by the Landau-level structure of charged pions. For physically relevant magnetic fields, this anisotropy reaches $\sim 10 - 15 \%$ at $T\simeq0.16$ GeV. The ratio of electric-charge susceptibility can be expressed as $\chi_4^Q/\chi_2^Q=C_4^Q/C_2^Q=\kappa_Q\sigma_Q^2$, where $C_2^Q$ and $C_4^Q$ are the second- and fourth-order cumulants, and $\kappa_Q$ and $\sigma_Q$ are the kurtosis and variance of the event-by-event net-electric-charge distribution. The reaction-plane dependence of this ratio provides an experimentally accessible signature of magnetic-field-induced anisotropy. Our results identify higher-order electric-charge fluctuations as a promising probe of the imprint of strong electromagnetic fields on the matter produced in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC.

hep-ph.title: $χ_{c1}(4010)$ as a $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ Molecular State: Mass, Decay Constant, and Width
hep-ph.author: S. Damen, H. Sundu, J.Y. Süngü
hep-ph.abstract: The charmonium-like state $\chi_{c1}(4010)$, recently observed by the LHCb Collaboration in $B^+ \to D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}K^+$ decays, is investigated as an axial-vector $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ molecular state within the QCD sum rule approach. A two-point sum rule incorporating quark, gluon, and mixed vacuum condensates up to dimension $10$ yields the mass and decay constant, $m_{\chi_{c1}(4010)} = (4005.89 \pm 47.15)~\text{MeV}$ and $f_{\chi_{c1}(4010)} = (2.87 \pm 0.55)\times 10^{-3}~\text{GeV}^{4}$, in agreement with the LHCb measurement. Since this mass lies above the $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ threshold, the strong coupling constants at the $\chi_{c1}(4010)D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ vertices are extracted from three-point sum rules and used to compute the partial widths of the $D^{*-}D^{+}$ and $D^{*+}D^{-}$ channels. The resulting total width, $\Gamma_{\chi_{c1}(4010)} = (57.64 \pm 9.64)~\text{MeV}$, is compatible with experiment within uncertainties. These results support a $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ molecular interpretation of $\chi_{c1}(4010)$ and offer sum-rule predictions for comparison with future measurements at BESIII, LHCb, and Belle~II.

hep-ph.title: $ψ(3S)$ and $η_c(3S)$ production in the $B^+$ decay processes
hep-ph.author: Zhuo Yu, Qi Wu, Man-Yu Duan, Zhou Rui, Dian-Yong Chen
hep-ph.abstract: In the present work, we investigate the production of psi(4040) in the B+ -> K+ psi(4040) process. Our estimations indicate that the unexpectedly large branching fraction could be well reproduced by taking both the short-range perturbative and long-range non-perturbative QCD contributions into account, where the long-range non-perturbative part plays an important role. Considering the structural similarity of eta_c(3S) and psi(3S), we apply the same model parameters to investigate the production of eta_c(3S) in the B+ decay process, and the branching fraction is predicted to be (0.81 +0.31 -0.29) x 10^-3. Based on the estimations in the present work and the relevant experimental measurements, we suggest that the experimentalists search for eta_c(3S) in the J/psi omega invariant mass distributions of B+ -> J/psi omega K+ process at Belle II and LHCb Collaborations.

hep-ph.title: Neural Network Representation of Generalized Parton Distributions (NNGPD)
hep-ph.author: Simonetta Liuti, Jitao Xu, Ho Jang, Zaki Panjsheeri, Gia-Wei Chern, Yaohang Li, Douglas Q. Adams, Michael Engelhardt, Gary R. Goldstein, Adil Khawaja, Huey-Wen Lin, Saraswati Pandey, Kemal Tezgin
hep-ph.abstract: Extracting generalized parton distributions (GPDs) from experimental observables, the convolution structures denoted as Compton form factors (CFFs), requires solving an intrinsic inverse problem. We presented results using NNGPD, a flexible regression method based on a physics-informed neural-network framework, for reconstructing GPDs using integral constraints -- including CFFs and Mellin moments -- and symmetry and endpoint constraints. The approach does not require pointwise training information on the underlying GPDs. Closure tests using pseudodata generated from a phenomenological model demonstrate the ability of the framework to reproduce the principal features of the underlying distributions across a range of kinematics. A Bayesian neural-network formulation is also introduced to address uncertainties associated with the reconstruction. Finally, we discussed a broader question in GPD phenomenology: whether the complete momentum-fraction dependence of GPDs is necessary to extract physical quantities such as partonic angular momentum. This motivates investigating approaches that infer Mellin moments directly from experimentally constrained CFFs, while quantifying the remaining ambiguities.

hep-ph.title: Regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics and non-perturbative renormalization of the shear viscosity of incompressible fluids
hep-ph.author: Mattis Harhoff, Cedric Riedel, Johannes Roth, Sören Schlichting
hep-ph.abstract: We propose a regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics that preserves all relevant symmetries. By considering an incompressible fluid, we demonstrate explicitly that the regularized theory is UV finite, and therefore admits a continuum limit. Strikingly, the regularized theory of stochastic fluid dynamics is not only amenable to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory, but also to functional methods in the continuum. We exploit this to perform renormalization group improved perturbative calculations of the renormalization of the shear viscosity of an incompressible fluid in two and three spatial dimensions, and compare our results to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory.

hep-ph.title: Neutrino Anomalies and Tensions: Experimental Status and Theoretical Interpretations
hep-ph.author: Doris Barčot, Raoul Serao, Antonio Capolupo
hep-ph.abstract: Neutrino oscillations successfully describe flavor conversion across a wide range of experiments, yet the origin of several excesses and deficits remains unresolved. This review connects these observations and long-baseline parameter tensions to their proposed physical explanations, clarifying what remains open and how it can be tested. We examine reactor and gallium measurements, accelerator appearance and disappearance searches, and atmospheric constraints, focusing on sterile neutrinos, non-standard interactions, and decoherence in open-system dynamics. For each mechanism, we assess what it modifies, which observations it can address, and which theoretical assumptions and independent constraints limit its viability. Recent results have restricted several interpretations and weakened some earlier tensions; no single extension provides an uncontested account of all observations. We identify the flavor, baseline, energy, and event-topology signatures needed to distinguish competing explanations and assess whether the remaining anomalies require new physics or reflect unresolved flux, interaction, and detector uncertainties.

hep-ph.title: Principle of no paradoxical Universe
hep-ph.author: Ngo Phuc Duc Loc
hep-ph.abstract: In the standard $\Lambda\rm CDM$ model, the Universe will keep expanding forever and its lifetime is infinite. Therefore, even the heaviest supermassive black hole will eventually evaporate and the universal occurrence of the black hole information paradox is unavoidable. However, the recent DESI results seem to indicate that dark energy is dynamical and, more importantly, it is possible that the Universe has a finite lifetime and will experience a ``Big Crunch" in some billion years from now. In light of this, the lightest confirmed black hole with mass of order one solar mass may not have a chance to evaporate before the Universe ends. Inspired by these observations, we thus raise an intriguing conjecture: Does the Universe choose a configuration such that the ``in-principle" black hole information paradox can never actually happen in reality? We derive a lower bound on black hole mass as a function of the Universe's lifetime such that the information paradox cannot be realized in nature and some resulting predictions are made. Some profound implications for other related big ideas in physics are briefly discussed.

hep-ph.title: Mass, forces, and the dark sector in a Kaluza-Klein model with 6 compact dimensions
hep-ph.author: Manfred M. Vieten
hep-ph.abstract: (1) Objective: This study seeks to calculate the meson and baryon masses and to investigate the dynamics within hadrons and lepton pairs by formulating a unified physical framework that, in addition to gravitation, simultaneously incorporates the strong, electromagnetic and weak interactions. (2) Method: A framework inspired by the Standard Model and based on Kaluza-Klein theory is formulated using an extended general-relativistic description in a spacetime of one temporal, three spatial, and six compactified dimensions. The model suggests that excitations, deformations of the 10-dimensional spacetime traveling at light-speed, contribute to mass and distinct spin characteristics in a 4-dimensional setting. Using the electron g-factor, charged-lepton masses, and masses of the proton, neutron, and neutral and charged pion, neutral and charged rho, phi, psi, upsilon mesons, the parameters compactification radius rho, weak interaction coupling alpha_w, strong interaction coupling alpha_s, flavor constants A_i and the antineutrino/neutrino density ratio delta3 are determined and used to compute the masses of the hadrons. (3) Key results: Masses of 102 hadrons are obtained; comparison with data from 71 measurements shows relative errors below 0.05 in 70%, below 0.1 in 89% and below 0.2 in 100%, with a correlation coefficient r=0.997 between the measured and calculated masses. Thirty-one additional hadron masses are predicted, and the model identifies asymmetries in electric and weak forces, as well as distance- and velocity-dependent interactions. (4) Implications: The framework offers testable predictions for hadron spectroscopy, predicts sterile, exclusive gravitationally interacting bosons as dark-matter candidates, states the equations for the elementary forces, and suggests possible connections between force asymmetries and dark energy.

hep-ph.title: Hidden Sector Relic Abundances from an Effective Planck Mass
hep-ph.author: Donald Liveoak, Anshuman Maharana, James D. Wells
hep-ph.abstract: Hidden sectors are generic in beyond the Standard Model constructions and string compactifications. We consider models featuring hidden sectors that have dark matter candidates. The relic density is set in part by the energy-injecting inflaton branching ratio $B$ to the sector. We develop a general framework to determine the dependence on $B$ for thermalized hidden sectors by defining an effective Planck mass for the Boltzmann equations for the hidden sector degrees of freedom. We apply this framework to several representative examples, including freeze-out/freeze-in WIMPs and multi-component dark matter. We find that the fractional energy density carried by freeze-out relics (in both single and multi-component models) and monopoles produced from second order phase transitions scale as $B^{1/4}$ and thus may lead to an overclosure problem, even with $B \ll 1$. On the other hand, the energy density of freeze-in relics scales as $B^{5/4}$ and is thus cosmologically irrelevant for sufficiently small $B$. Finally, we discuss the cumulative implications of a large number of hidden sectors.

hep-ph.title: Equiprobability Anomaly Detector Using Angular Distributions
hep-ph.author: Alex Whitten, John Cicero, Tae Min Hong
hep-ph.abstract: We use the angular distribution of top quark pairs ($t\bar{t}$) in the semileptonic final state $b\bar{b}\,\ell\nu q\bar{q}'$ to construct an anomaly detector for non-$t\bar{t}$ events. Wigner $D$ functions expand the distribution with coefficients determined by orthogonal series density estimation. Its equiprobable surfaces bin the events, the non-$t\bar{t}$ concentrate at low $t\bar{t}$ density. The separation is quantified by the Kullback-Leibler divergence, which makes connection to variational autoencoders. The performance is comparable to normalizing flows at parton level, but is limited by jet assignments at reconstruction level.

hep-ph.title: Complete $g^6$ pressure of hot Yang-Mills theory
hep-ph.author: Keijo Kajantie, Pablo Navarrete, Risto Paatelainen, Leon Sandbote, York Schröder, Kaapo Seppänen, Aleksi Vuorinen
hep-ph.abstract: We present the full order $g^6$ term in the weak-coupling expansion of the pressure of hot $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Yang-Mills theory, resolving a problem that has remained open for more than two decades. To achieve this, we evaluate nine previously unknown nonfactorizing four-loop sum-integrals using the thermal loop-tree duality method with novel local ultraviolet and infrared subtractions, thereby completing the hard-scale contribution to the pressure for general $\mathrm{SU}(N_c)$. Combining this result with known chromoelectric and chromomagnetic contributions, available for $N_c=3$, we demonstrate the analytic cancellation of infrared divergences originating from different momentum scales and obtain the complete $O(g^6)$ pressure for $\mathrm{SU}(3)$. Our result displays quantitative agreement with data from four-dimensional lattice simulations over a broad range of temperatures, providing a stringent test of the dimensionally reduced effective-field-theory paradigm.

hep-ph.title: The pressure of the gluon plasma at $\mathcal{O}(g_s^6)$, perturbatively
hep-ph.author: Mikael Chala, Luis Gil, Javier López Miras
hep-ph.abstract: We determine the four-loop hard-scale matching correction to the pressure of the gluon plasma at high temperature. This result completes the long-standing calculation through $\mathcal{O}(g_s^6)$, where $g_s$ is the strong coupling. Our result agrees, within uncertainties, with the value obtained inarXiv:1204.6184by fitting the perturbative series to continuum-extrapolated lattice data, thereby providing the first direct test of the weak-coupling expansion at this order.

hep-ph.title: Exploring QCD Matter through Energy Correlators of Soft Hadrons
hep-ph.author: Yiyang Peng, João Barata, Andrey V. Sadofyev, Huichao Song
hep-ph.abstract: We propose energy-energy correlators (EECs) of soft hadrons and their azimuthal harmonics as new soft observables to probe the collective flow and correlations beyond flow for large and small systems created in high energy nuclear collisions. We separate the soft EEC into a disconnected contribution determined by the mean energy flow and a connected contribution encoding correlations beyond it. Viscous hydrodynamic simulations demonstrate that the soft EEC of a fluid system is governed by the disconnected contribution, while its elliptic and triangular harmonics respond to the initial geometry and shear viscosity as traditional flow harmonics do. Comparisons between iEBE-VISHNU and PYTHIA for p+p, O+O, and Pb+Pb collisions show that the disconnected contribution dominates at large angles in all systems, whereas connected correlations beyond the mean energy flow grow toward small angles and small systems, most strongly for the harmonics. Soft EECs thus provide a unique window into collective flow and correlations beyond it across collision systems.

hep-ph.title: Hidden Supersymmetry in AdS/QCD models for Fermions
hep-ph.author: Rafael A. Costa-Silva, Henrique Boschi-Filho
hep-ph.abstract: We show that the chiral modes splitted from the Dirac equation satisfying Schrodinger-like equations in the context of deformed AdS/QCD model are isospectral, since the chiral effective potentials are SUSY partners. In particular, we show how to perform truncations of these potentials that preserve isospectrality of the chiral modes. Following this prescription, we compare a quadratic approximation of the deformed AdS model with the dressed soft wall model for fermions and show how the spectra of both models can coincide.

hep-ph.title: $NΛ$ interaction from a quark model: $pΛ$ femtoscopy and the hypertriton
hep-ph.author: Ye Yan, Qian Wu, Qi Huang, Hongxia Huang, Jialun Ping
hep-ph.abstract: Understanding the low-energy nucleon--$\Lambda$ interaction is essential for describing hypernuclear structures, while its spin dependence remains insufficiently constrained by experimental data. In this work, we investigate the $N\Lambda$ interaction using the quark delocalization color screening model and explore its implications for $p\Lambda$ femtoscopy and the hypertriton. The energy and scattering phase shifts of the $N\Lambda$ system are calculated, revealing weak attraction in both the $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ channels, but no bound states. The corresponding scattering lengths and effective ranges are found to be $-2.36$ fm and $1.61$ fm for $J^P=0^+$, and $-0.95$ fm and $1.46$ fm for $J^P=1^+$, respectively. Using the Gel'fand--Levitan--Marchenko inverse-scattering method, effective $N\Lambda$ potentials are reconstructed from the coupled-channel scattering phase shifts and applied to calculate the $p\Lambda$ femtoscopic correlation function. Comparison with experimental data suggests that the spin-triplet attraction may be underestimated in the present model. Furthermore, employing the Gaussian Expansion Method, we investigate the $NN\Lambda$ three-body system and obtain a weakly bound hypertriton with a $\Lambda$ separation energy of $1.06$--$1.16$ MeV. These results demonstrate that $p\Lambda$ femtoscopic correlations and hypertriton binding provide complementary probes of the spin-dependent $N\Lambda$ interaction, offering valuable constraints on its low-energy behavior.

hep-ph.title: Consistency Checks for Λ positive Quantum Cosmology
hep-ph.author: S. P. Miao, N. C. Tsamis, R. P. Woodard
hep-ph.abstract: In this paper we improve and further analyze the recently derived quantum gravity equations which apply in accelerating cosmological spacetimes and whose solutions re-sum leading logarithms from all orders of perturbation theory. We show the consistency of these upgraded equations against 1-loop non-trivial exact perturbative computations. The upgraded equations retain their remarkably simple form.

hep-ph.title: Gauge-Covariant Wavelets for Quark-Propagator Sparsening and Distillation in Lattice QCD
hep-ph.author: Debsubhra Chakraborty, Nilmani Mathur, Mrinmoy Basak
hep-ph.abstract: We develop a novel gauge-covariant wavelet framework for computing hadronic correlation functions in lattice QCD. Two complementary approaches connect spatial localization and resolution-scale separation to propagator sparsening and distillation. A gauge-covariant fast wavelet transform, based on compactly supported biorthogonal filters, coarse-grains quark propagators and reduces early-time excited-state contamination relative to direct decimation at equal spatial reduction. A second construction applies a resolvent filter of the spatial covariant Laplacian to localized sources, generating a distillation subspace without computing Laplacian eigenpairs. We detail its gauge covariance, smearing profiles, and implementation in exact and stochastic distillation. Spatial localization enables unbiased Hansen-Hurwitz sampling of hadronic contractions, reducing their computational cost substantially. We also examine momentum aliasing induced by fixed coarse grids and the use of random grid shifts to remove unwanted contributions in expectation. Numerical benchmarks of the proposed methods are performed with single hadrons, the I = 2 two-pion system, the deuteron channel, and boosted nucleons. The extracted energy levels agree very well with full or conventional distillation calculations within statistical uncertainties. We quantify the costs of on-demand basis construction and contractions, demonstrate contraction speedups at comparable statistical precision. These studies establish a practical foundation of wavelet-based propagator compression and operator construction for multi-operator calculations of hadronic and nuclear systems, particularly at larger lattice volumes.

hep-ph.title: Two-nucleon scattering amplitudes at light quark masses from lattice QCD
hep-ph.author: Jorge Baeza-Ballesteros, André Baião-Raposo, Davide Laudicina, Malcolm Lazarow, Miguel Salg, John Bulava, Jeremy R. Green, Andrew Hanlon, Renwick J. Hudspith, Daniel Mohler, Colin Morningstar, Amy Nicholson, Fernando Romero-López, Thomas R. Richardson, André Walker-Loud, Hartmut Wittig, for theBaryon Scattering(BaSc)Collaboration
hep-ph.abstract: We present a lattice-QCD determination of nucleon-nucleon scattering amplitudes at pion masses of $M_\pi \approx 200$ MeV and $M_\pi \approx 280$ MeV at a single lattice spacing $a \approx 0.064$ fm on two CLS ensembles. The finite-volume energy spectra are extracted from large Hermitian correlation matrices constructed within the distillation framework using an extensive basis of two-nucleon interpolating operators. To reliably relate the finite-volume spectra to the infinite-volume scattering amplitudes, we employ two recently developed formalisms that explicitly account for the long-range interaction generated by one-pion exchange: the plane-wave quantization condition and the relativistic left-hand-cut formalism. We discuss the quark-mass dependence of the nucleon-nucleon scattering lengths, effective ranges, shape parameters and pole positions. At all pion masses considered, our analysis prefers virtual states in both isospin channels by more than $1\sigma$. Comparing also results from our previous calculation at $M_\pi \approx 710$ MeV, we observe that the inverse scattering lengths and binding momenta approach their physical-point phenomenological values monotonically as the pion mass is varied.

hep-ph.title: Spinors, Doppelgängers and the Non-Perturbative Classical Double Copy
hep-ph.author: Kymani Armstrong-Williams
hep-ph.abstract: We develop a geometric and spinorial formulation of the non-perturbative classical double copy between the Corrigan--Fairlie--'t Hooft--Wilczek sector of complexified SU(2) Yang--Mills theory and four-dimensional conformally flat gravity. We identify the gauge potential with the positive-chiral spin connection of the conformally flat metric, establishing an exact relation between the Yang--Mills field strength and the chiral projection of the Riemann tensor. This provides a four-dimensional realisation of the doppelgänger viewpoint, in which gauge and gravitational fields arise from different interpretations of common connection data. Within this sector, the sourceless Yang--Mills equations require constant scalar curvature, explaining the shared nonlinear scalar equation and extending the gravitational correspondence from traceless matter to matter with constant energy--momentum trace. By representing adjoint colour indices as symmetric pairs of spinor indices, we derive exact relations mapping the gauge field-strength spinors to the scalar-curvature and trace-free Ricci components of the gravitational curvature. These relations retain nontrivial curvature information despite the vanishing Weyl tensor. We illustrate the construction using anti-de Sitter and de Sitter spacetimes, together with $\mathrm{AdS}_{3}\times\mathbb{R}$ supported by a scalar field, demonstrating the extension to matter with nonzero constant trace

hep-ph.title: Effects of kinematic cuts on $v_0(p_T)$
hep-ph.author: Tribhuban Parida, Rupam Samanta, Jean-Yves Ollitrault
hep-ph.abstract: We show that the analysis of $v_0(p_T)$ is biased when low-$p_T$ particles are not detected. The low-$p_T$ threshold shifts $v_0(p_T)$ by a constant negative value, which depends on the threshold. We evaluate the shift using hydrodynamic simulations. Correcting for this bias significantly improves agreement between ALICE and ATLAS results for $v_0(p_T)$ in Pb+Pb collisions.

hep-ph.title: The metric-affine $\mathring{R}^2$ scalaron: parameter-free inflation
hep-ph.author: Christian Dioguardi
hep-ph.abstract: We present a model of slow-roll inflation in metric-affine gravity, where the connection is independent of the metric. We require that the Einstein-Hilbert term is the only operator that breaks three out of four shift-symmetries of the connection, and impose them on the metric-affine Starobinsky term $\alpha R(\Gamma)^2$. This replaces it by $\alpha\mathring{R}^2$, the square of the invariant part of the scalar curvature. The theory propagates only the graviton and one healthy scalar, the metric-affine $\mathring{R}^2$ scalaron. Its potential approaches a plateau polynomially, $U\simeq U_0(1-\mu^2/\chi^2)$, with $\mu=\sqrt{6}\,M_P$ fixed by the curvature of the connection. Once $\alpha\simeq2\times10^{8}$ is set by the scalar amplitude, the model has no free parameters. It predicts $n_s\simeq1-3/(2N_*)$ and $r\simeq2\sqrt3\,N_*^{-3/2}$ at leading order in $N_*$, and $n_s=0.968$--$0.974$ and $r=0.011$-$0.008$ with exact slow-roll for $N_*=50$-$60$ $e$-folds. These values agree with current data, and $r$ is within reach of the next generation of $B$-mode measurements.

hep-ph.title: Impact of Irrep Truncations on Quantum Simulations of QCD
hep-ph.author: Patrick Draper, Drishti Gupta
hep-ph.abstract: Quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories with continuous gauge groups require a choice of basis (how states of the gauge theory map to the qubit computational basis) and truncation scheme (which of the infinitely many gauge theory basis states should be omitted in the map to the finite dimensional qubit Hilbert space.) The most common choices are adapted to an electric basis for the gauge theory, where the basis states for each link are associated with irreducible representations of the gauge group. Electric bases and truncations are generally advantageous for preserving gauge symmetries and simulating the strong coupling regime, but their effectiveness in the weak coupling regimes of physical interest are less well understood. In this work, we compute relative probabilities $p(R')/p(R)$ for finding a link in the irreps $R,R'$ in the ground state of SU(3) lattice gauge theory using Euclidean Monte Carlo methods and weak-coupling lattice perturbation theory. The observables that compute these relative probabilities are constructed by introducing seams into an anisotropic lattice, and by a similar construction we are also able to measure relative probabilities of different site singlets (ways that electric flux braids together into a gauge singlet) at each vertex. With these methods we can quantify, for example, the importance of higher electric flux states in the weak coupling ground state. These results directly inform what truncations are needed to accurately capture non-abelian gauge dynamics near the continuum limit.

hep-ph.title: Foreground dependence of the 20 GeV Galactic halo gamma-ray excess and its proposed connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN event
hep-ph.author: Kevork N. Abazajian, Youyou Li, Oscar Macias
hep-ph.abstract: We assess the dark matter interpretation of the 20 GeV gamma-ray halo excess reported by Totani and its proposed connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) high-energy nuclear-recoil event, which independently favors dark matter masses above about 200 GeV. Using fifteen years of Fermi-LAT data, we reproduce the excess under the original assumptions and test it against 281 Galactic diffuse emission configurations, three descriptions of the Fermi bubbles, four of Loop I, and uniform and X-ray-brightness-weighted eROSITA bubbles templates. A component correlated with a Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) annihilation template remains with finer spatial binning and the instrumental response included. Outside the Fermi bubbles footprint, it is detected at nominal significances of about 4-16$\sigma$ over 5.6-130 GeV, falling to 1-7$\sigma$ when the enlarged boundaries of a recent substructured bubbles model are also excluded. With the substructured model, which improves the fit substantially, the component remains at 7-18$\sigma$ in four of six representative foreground configurations. However, its amplitude and spectrum depend strongly on the foreground model, and no tested foreground yields a single NFW normalization across the sky, including with additional spatial freedom in the eROSITA bubbles. Simulations show that foreground mismodeling can produce spurious NFW-correlated emission of the observed amplitude, and that residual-derived bubbles templates can bias the recovered spectrum. The 420 GeV $W^+W^-$ spectrum motivated by the LZ connection describes the data for some foreground models but is disfavored by others. These results disfavor interpreting the full excess as annihilation in a smooth NFW halo and weaken the case for a common origin with the LZ event, but they do not exclude a dark matter contribution to the persistent halo-like residual. [abridged]

hep-ph.title: Gravitational Waves as a Probe of Multi-Fluid Cosmologies: General Formalism and the Case of Cosmological Stasis
hep-ph.author: Keith R. Dienes, Fazlollah Hajkarim, Lucien Heurtier, Fei Huang, Kuver Sinha, Brooks Thomas, Tao Xu
hep-ph.abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) provide a powerful probe of the expansion history of the universe prior to the Big Bang. Indeed, the production of such gravity waves depends on the evolution of first-order scalar perturbations within the early universe, while their subsequent propagation depends on the background equation of state. In this paper we extend previous discussions by studying SIGWs in cosmologies containing multiple fluids. As we shall demonstrate, the gravitational-wave signal within such multi-fluid cosmologies is modified in two distinct ways: not only are there new velocity effects which have no single-fluid analogues, but there are also significant alterations to the subsequent redshifting of modes that enter the horizon before the multi-fluid era ends. Thus SIGWs provide a probe of not only the overall expansion rate within such cosmologies, but also their internal multi-fluid composition. As an example, we then consider the case of gravitational waves arising during an epoch of cosmological stasis. During such an epoch, the abundances of energy components with different equations of state remain constant, thereby giving rise to a universe with a constant effective equation of state which nevertheless remains genuinely multi-fluid despite cosmological expansion. Despite their constant equations of state, we find that such stasis cosmologies also give rise to tensor power spectra and present-day gravitational-wave abundances which are significantly different from those expected within a standard radiation-dominated universe.

hep-ph.title: Reference frame dependence of the periodically oscillating Coulomb field in the Proca theory
hep-ph.author: Bogdan Damski
hep-ph.abstract: The Proca theory of the real massive vector field admits non-equilibrium solutions, where the asymptotic dynamics of its electric field is dominated by the periodically oscillating Coulomb component. We discuss how such field configurations are seen in different reference frames, where we find an intriguing spatial pattern of the vector field of the Proca theory and the electromagnetic field associated with it.

hep-ph.title: Bayesian inference of the magnetic component of quark-gluon plasma
hep-ph.author: Yu Guo, Jinfeng Liao, Shuzhe Shi
hep-ph.abstract: The chromo-magnetic monopoles (CMM), emergent topological excitations of non-Abelian gauge fields carrying chromo-magnetic charge, have long been postulated to play an important role in the vacuum confinement of quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the deconfinement transition at temperature $T_c\approx 160\rm MeV$, as well as the strongly coupled nature of quark-gluon plasma (QGP). While such CMMs have been found to provide solutions for challenging puzzles from heavy-ion collision measurements, they were typically introduced as model assumptions in the past. Here we show how their very existence can be determined and their abundance extracted in a data-driven way for the first time. Using the \textsc{cujet3} framework for calculations of jet energy loss and analyzing a comprehensive experimental data set for nuclear modification factor ($R_{\mathrm{AA}}$) and elliptic flow ($v_2$) of high-transverse-momentum hadrons, the fraction of CMMs in the QGP is obtained by Bayesian inference and is found to be substantial in the $1\sim 2 T_c$ region. The posterior CMM fraction is further validated by excellent agreement with additional data and is also shown to predict QGP transport properties quantitatively consistent with the state-of-the-art knowledge.

hep-ph.title: Dark Photon mediated Inelastic Dark Matter in Cosmology, Astrophysics and Colliders
hep-ph.author: Abhishek Roy, Prasenjit Sanyal, Stefano Scopel(CQUeST, Seoul and Sogang U.)
hep-ph.abstract: We explore the phenomenology of Dark Photon iDM ($A^\prime$IDM) where the Standard Model (SM) is extended by a dark sector containing an additional $U(1)_D$ gauge symmetry with coupling $\alpha_D$ under which all SM particles are neutral, and that couples to the SM hypercharge gauge boson through a kinetic mixing parameter $\epsilon$. The model contains two Majorana states $\chi_1$ and $\chi_2$ with $\delta=M_{\chi_2}-M_{\chi_1}>0$ and $\chi_1$ the dark matter candidate, and a dark photon $A^{\prime}$ with mass $M_{A^{\prime}}$. Our analysis represents an integration of existing ones, where only specific benchmarks of the A'IDM scenario have been discussed. We perform a complete scan of the parameters of the model ($M_{\chi_1}$, $\delta$, $M_{A^{\prime}}$, $\epsilon$, $\alpha_D$) and discuss the $\chi_1$ relic abundance, its direct and indirect searches, as well as potential signals from astrophysics and accelerators. Our scan shows that $\alpha_D=\alpha_{EM}$ is not disfavored, as some previous analyses, limited to specific benchmarks, may suggest. We also find that when the $\chi_1$ relic density matches observation direct and indirect searches are not kinematically accessible. On the other hand we find that the projected luminosity of FASER, a detector searching for Long Lived Particles (LLP) decay at the LHC, can probe or rule out the parameters space of the model for $M_{\chi_1}\lesssim$ 7 GeV, 100 MeV$\lesssim\delta\lesssim$300 MeV and $M_{A^\prime}\lesssim$25 GeV. This range of parameter could be significantly extended by the FASER 2 upgrade proposed for the High-Luminosity phase at the LHC. The parameter space probed by LLP seaches partially overlaps with that probed by $\chi_1$ capture in neutron stars.

hep-ph.title: Gamma-Ray Signatures of Thermal Misalignment Dark Matter
hep-ph.author: Koichi Hamaguchi, Ryoichiro Hayakawa, Hiroki Takahashi
hep-ph.abstract: Thermal misalignment is a viable dark matter scenario where the misalignment of a dark matter scalar, feebly coupled to the Standard Model particles, is generated through thermal effects from the primordial plasma. In this framework, the scalar is generically metastable, and its decay can leave observable signatures. In this work, we focus on the case in which the scalar $\phi$ is coupled to photons through $\phi F^{\mu\nu} F_{\mu\nu}$, and examine its observational signatures. We find that current gamma-ray constraints place a robust upper bound on the scalar mass of $\mathcal O(1)\,\mathrm{GeV}$. We also find that future observations can further probe the parameter region, particularly in the MeV-GeV range, an energy band expected to be explored by various gamma-ray observatories in the coming decades.

hep-ph.title: A New Look at the X Compositeness from its Lineshape
hep-ph.author: A. Carducci, G. Cianti, P. D'Annibali, D. Germani, A.D. Polosa
hep-ph.abstract: Available data on the $X(3872)$ lineshape have been fitted with a Flattè parametrization derived from an effective Lagrangian in which $X$, $D$, and $D^*$ are all elementary fields. A molecular $X$, i.e., a deuteron-like bound state of $D$ and $\bar{D}^*$, must instead be described by an effective theory where the $X$ field is initially absent or introduced as an auxiliary, unphysical, field, yielding a lineshape parametrization that differs significantly from the Flattè one. We demonstrate, in the analogous theory of nucleons with an auxiliary deuteron field, that this parametrization gives a fully consistent description of $np\to\text{deuteron}\to np$ scattering data, and motivate applying the same method to the $X$ lineshape. The analysis proposed here is novel and has not previously been carried out on the available data.

hep-ph.title: Correlated $b \to s$ and $s \to d$ Rare Semileptonic Transitions in the Standard Model Effective Field Theory

hep-ph.title: Single inclusive hadron and jet production in lepton-hadron scattering
hep-ph.author: Jian-Wei Qiu, Kazuhiro Watanabe
hep-ph.abstract: We present the first calculation of single inclusive hadron and jet production at large transverse momentum in lepton-hadron scattering in a joint QCD+QED factorization approach. The scattering cross section is factorized into a convolution of infrared-safe hard coefficient functions with universal lepton distribution functions (LDFs) and parton distribution functions (PDFs) of the colliding lepton and hadron, respectively, together with fragmentation functions (FFs) of the observed hadron (or jet). With joint QCD+QED factorization, the Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) type evolution equations for LDFs, PDFs, and FFs necessarily have evolution kernels calculated in both QCD and QED. We derive a default set of LDFs for our calculations and discuss a strategy to extract universal, non-perturbative LDFs from future data. We present our calculations for single inclusive hadron and/or jet production at the energies of Jefferson Lab and the future Electron-Ion Collider.

hep-ph.title: Probing Quantum Foundations in Long-Baseline Neutrino Oscillations: Wave Packet Approach from MINOS Data to DUNE Predictions
hep-ph.author: Baktiar Wasir Farooq, Bipin Singh Koranga, Massimo Blasone
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate neutrino flavor oscillations in the wave packet formalism, extending the standard planewave treatment to incorporate the finite spatial coherence of neutrino massthis http URLderive the full three flavor oscillation probability with MSW matter effects, decoherence, and localization suppression governed by the wave packet width, benchmarking against MINOS disappearance data and extending to DUNE predictions under the same parameters. To quantify how sharply the oscillation data constrain the wave packet width, we compute the classical Fisher information FC as a function of neutrino energy for both MINOS and DUNE, and show that its sensitivity is concentrated precisely in the low-energy regime where the wave-packet and plane-wave predictions diverge. Beyond the oscillation probability analysis, we compute wave particle entanglement complementarity quantities within a quantum information theoretic framework and explore the complete triality description involving entanglement, predictability, and visibility as functions of neutrino energy for both experiments such as MINOS and DUNE. We show that even when the oscillation probability is numerically indistinguishable from the planewave result, the wave packet structure leaves observable imprints in these triality measures. Our results demonstrate that the wave packet approach provides a theoretically consistent and experimentally motivated framework for probing quantum foundations in long-baseline atmospheric neutrino oscillation experiments.

hep-ph.title: Reassessing the $X(2370)$ in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$ beyond the one-dimensional mass projections
hep-ph.author: Xiang-Kun Dong, Teng Ji, Meike Küßner, Ulf-G. Meißner
hep-ph.abstract: The BESIII Collaboration recently extracted the properties of the $X(2370)$ from a fit to the one-dimensional $K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$ invariant-mass spectrum in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$. The intermediate two-body structures visible in the mass correlations, including the $K_0^*(1430)$ bands, require a coherent treatment of cross-channel interference when interpreting the enhancement near 2.3 GeV. We reassess the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution by fitting the published data using an effective coupled-channel framework with an approximate detection efficiency depending on the three-body invariant mass. The three-body parent amplitude is parameterized using a $K$-matrix that describes scattering among several quasi-two-body channels. The seven- and eight-bare-state models give similar mass distributions. Adding the eighth bare state lowers the Poisson deviance by 1.22% and produces an additional pole at $E=(2419-i152)$ MeV, substantially broader than the $X(2370)$ mass-width reference. This pole is model-dependent, and its identification with the $X(2370)$ is not clear. The present analysis does not establish the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$, thereby weakening the flavor-singlet argument based on the suppression of $K^*\bar K$ relative to the total $K\bar K\pi$ contribution. A more comprehensive experimental amplitude analysis, incorporating coherent interference, mass and angular correlations, and detector effects across related decay channels, is needed to establish the role and decay properties of the $X(2370)$.

hep-ph.title: Polar Angle Dependence of the Alignment Polarization of Quarks Produced in $e^+e^-$ Annihilation
hep-ph.author: S. Groote, J.G. Körner, M.M. Tung
hep-ph.abstract: We calculate one-loop radiative QCD corrections to the three polarized and unpolarized structure functions that determine the beam-quark polar angle dependence of the alignment (or longitudinal) polarization of light and heavy quarks produced in $e^+e^-$ annihilations. We present analytical and numerical results for the alignment polarization and its polar angle dependence. We discuss in some detail the zero-mass limit of our results and the role of the anomalous spin-flip contributions to the polarization observables in the zero-mass limit. Our discussion includes transverse and longitudinal beam polarization effects.

hep-ph.title: Graded transcendental functions: an application to four-point amplitudes with one off-shell leg
hep-ph.author: Thomas Gehrmann, Johannes Henn, Petr Jakubčík, Jungwon Lim, Cesare Carlo Mella, Nikolaos Syrrakos, Lorenzo Tancredi, William J. Torres Bobadilla
hep-ph.abstract: Several recent works have demonstrated the powerful algebraic simplifications that can be achieved for scattering amplitudes through a systematic grading of transcendental quantities. We develop these concepts to construct a minimal basis of functions tailored to a scattering amplitude in a general way. Starting with formal solutions for all master integral topologies, we organise the appearing functions by properties such as their symbol alphabet or letter adjacency. We rotate the basis such that functions with spurious features appear in the least possible number of basis elements. Since their coefficients must vanish for physical quantities, this approach avoids complex cancellations. As a first application, we evaluate all integral topologies relevant to the three-loop $Hggg$ and $Hgq\bar{q}$ amplitudes in the leading-colour approximation and heavy-top limit. We describe the derivation of canonical differential equation systems and present a method for fixing boundary conditions without the need for a full functional representation. Using multiple numerical reductions, we test the maximal transcendentality conjecture for $Hggg$ and identify a new letter which appears in functions of weight 4 and 5. In addition, we provide the first direct analytic computation of a three-point form factor of the operator $\mathrm{Tr}(\phi^2)$ in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ sYM and find agreement with numerical and bootstrapped results.

hep-ph.title: Analytic formulae for non-local nonstabiliserness in bipartite systems of qutrits and ququints
hep-ph.author: Giorgio Busoni, John Gargalionis, Ewan N. V. Wallace, Martin J. White
hep-ph.abstract: We conjecture analytic expressions for the non-local magic of bipartite pure qudit states of prime local dimension. Our construction relies on the Schmidt-aligned state attaining the minimum over local unitaries, a hypothesis that we support with numerical evidence for pairs of qutrits and ququints. For composite local dimensions, we find that the analogous expressions do not in general reproduce the global minimum, but can still provide computationally cheap approximations to the non-local magic. We also find that relations between non-local magic and entanglement diagnostics that hold for two qubits generally do not extend to qutrit and higher-dimensional systems. As a few-body application, we evaluate the qutrit non-local magic generated by elastic pion scattering, treating hadronic isospin as the qutrit. We find that $p$-wave charged pion scattering realises the maximum non-local magic allowed in the system just below the $\rho$-meson resonance.

hep-ph.title: The Effect of Mass Loss and Convective Overshooting on the Pre-Collapse Structure, Composition, and Neutrino Emission of Red Supergiants
hep-ph.author: McKenzie A. Myers, Claire B. Campbell, Kelly M. Patton, Segev BenZvi, Marta Colomer Molla, Alec Habig, James P. Kneller, Dan Milisavljevic, Jeffrey Tseng
hep-ph.abstract: Prior to core collapse, the neutrino emission from red supergiants (RSGs) is so large that a nearby ($\lesssim1\:$kpc) RSG will become visible in current and near-future neutrino detectors. The rate of emission and the spectra of the pre-supernova (pre-SN) neutrinos from RSGs are sensitive to the temperature, density, and detailed isotopic composition of the core. During the last year of the star's life, these properties change considerably as the nuclear burning accelerates and deleptonization begins. Uncertainties in stellar evolution modeling - including the treatment of mass loss and convective overshooting - alter the thermal conditions and composition of the RSG core as it approaches collapse, and thus one expects a consequent effect upon the pre-SN emission. In this paper we present the first study of how varying the treatment of mass loss and convective overshooting together affects the pre-collapse core properties and neutrino emission of RSGs. We use the stellar evolution instrument MESA and construct a grid of 32 RSG models with zero-age main sequence masses of $\{ 12, 15, 18, 20\}$ M$_\odot$, apply the so-called "Dutch" mass-loss scheme with wind efficiencies of $\{0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.0\}$, and consider two convective overshooting schemes. Our models use a large 206-isotope nuclear network in order to accurately compute the structure and composition of the star. We find that varying the treatment of mass loss and overshooting results in significant differences in core properties and the strength and timing of shell burning episodes, and that the onset of silicon shell burning leads to a localized peak in the pre-SN neutrino event rate observed by a JUNO-like detector $\sim 10$ hours to $\sim 1$ hour prior to collapse.

hep-ph.title: Charged-current neutrino opacity within the relativistic Hartree-Fock framework for astrophysical simulations of core-collapse supernovae and binary neutron star mergers
hep-ph.author: Kamil Sokołowski, Anil Kumar, Tobias Fischer
hep-ph.abstract: Neutrinos and their weak interactions play a vital role in the physics of core-collapse supernovae and binary neutron star mergers. Their description within astrophysical simulations, including the weak rates, is of pivotal importance not only for the prediction of accurate neutrino fluxes and spectra, including the associated conditions relevant to nucleosynthesis, neutrinos are also responsible for heating and cooling of the stellar plasma as well as the transport of lepton number and entropy. In the present article, we develop an essential improvement of the description of the underlying nuclear medium, necessary for the calculations of charged-current weak rates, with the inclusion of explicitly momentum-dependent nuclear interactions. To this end, we introduce the relativistic Hartree-Fock (RHF) approach and the associated momentum-dependent nucleon self-energies. We discuss the resulting neutrino and antineutrino opacities and find large discrepancies comparing the weak rates at the RHF level with those of commonly used relativistic mean-field (RMF) models. In particular, we observe a substantial shift of previously reported large medium-dependent modifications associated with the RMF approach.

hep-ph.title: AgentRivet: an automated system for producing Rivet routines from journal publications
hep-ph.author: Antonio J. Costa, Caterina Doglioni, Christian Gütschow, Andrew D. Pilkington, Sukanya Sinha
hep-ph.abstract: Particle physics collider experiments provide Rivet routines as part of the analysis preservation strategy for model-independent measurements. Rivet is a C++ toolkit that allow new theoretical models to be compared to the measurements, thus aiding the development and tuning of Monte Carlo event generators as well as searches for physics beyond the Standard Model. However, analysis coverage is known to be incomplete, with only 39% of measurements having documented and publicly available Rivet routines. In this article, we design and implement an automated workflow based on Large Language Models with the goal of providing the missing routines. This multi-step workflow, referred to as AgentRivet, extracts the physics analysis information from published papers and writes the missing Rivet routines, with intermediate code- and physics- reviews as part of an autonomous quality control. We report the results obtained using commercial Large Language Models, provided by OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, for two recent measurements from the ATLAS and CMS experiments. We find that AgentRivet produces competent Rivet routines with few syntax errors. The physics fidelity of the routines is reasonable and follows the explanations given in the relevant publications. Nevertheless, physics-implementation issues do arise and are investigated using the artefacts produced by AgentRivet. The majority of physics implementation issues arise from subtle-but-ambiguous definitions in the given publication, although some models struggle to implement complex observables even when clear definitions are given.

hep-ph.title: Constraints from big bang nucleosynthesis and cosmological observations on varying Higgs vacuum expectation value
hep-ph.author: Hongrui Feng, Yudong Luo, Toshitaka Kajino, Bao-Hua Sun, Tatsushi Shima
hep-ph.abstract: The Higgs vacuum expectation value (VEV) alters both the electroweak and strong interaction rates. We study both effects on big bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) and seek concordance between observed primordial abundances of light elements and cosmological constraints from CMB fluctuations and anisotropies. We find a strong negative correlation between primordial 4He abundance and the Higgs VEV. Consequently, using a 1.58% uplift of the Higgs VEV during BBN from the current value, an agreement can be achieved among the new primordial 4He abundance, observed by the EMPRESS group, Deuterium abundance determined from absorption lines in the Lyman-alpha forest along the line-of-sight of high-redshift quasars, and the lithium abundance on the Spite plateau. This agreement requires a baryon-to-photon ratio different from the CMB determination, indicating the need for nonstandard cosmological evolution between BBN and recombination epochs. We also demonstrate that a 0.2% uplift in the Higgs VEV can partially alleviate the "cosmic Li problem," keeping consistency with the CMB with remaining discrepancy potentially accounted for by stellar depletion mechanisms.

hep-ph.title: Longitudinal $Λ$ polarization as a competition between freeze-out geometry and elliptic flow in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.36\,\mathrm{TeV}$
hep-ph.author: Yilong Xie, Simin Wu, Laszlo P. Csernai
hep-ph.abstract: The second sine harmonic $\Pz$ of longitudinal $\Lambda$ polarization is sensitive to the balance between the kinematic-vorticity contribution $\Pz^\omega$ and the kinematic-shear contribution $\Pz^\Xi$ at decoupling. We quantify this competition in a scan of 48 Pb-Pb initial states evolved with the (3+1)-dimensional Particle-In-Cell Relativistic (PICR) ideal-hydrodynamic code. With the isothermal local-equilibrium (ILE) prescription, the total harmonic follows $\Pz\simeq a\,\efo-b\,v_2$, with $a\simeq0.010$ and $b\simeq0.014$, where $\efo$ is the freeze-out eccentricity and $v_2$ the elliptic flow of $\Lambda$ hyperons. With coefficients fixed on these 48 states, the relation describes 86\% of the variation of $\Pz$ in 12 states outside the fit. To identify the origin of the two terms, we decompose the ILE integrand exactly into an emission-gradient term and a curl term. On the PICR decoupling surfaces, the tangential emission gradient is positive on average, correlates most strongly with $\efo$, and admits a surface-curvature representation, whereas the normal emission gradient and the curl term are negative on average and correlate most strongly with $v_2$. A blast-wave calculation with the same integrand gives coefficients of comparable magnitude and shows how the cancellation point $\efo/v_2=b/a$ changes with the flow and the surface geometry; both PICR and blast-wave calculations predict that $b/a$ rises with hadron mass from the proton to the $\Omega$ when the decoupling surface is held fixed. Although the geometry inferred from ALICE data depends on the background, the measured polarization constrains the displacement of $\efo$ from the cancellation boundary $\efo=(b/a)v_2$. For the central ALICE measurement values at $5.36\,\mathrm{TeV}$, the backgrounds examined give $\efo\simeq0.2$--$0.4$ in 30--50\% Pb-Pb collisions.

hep-lat.title: Gauge-Covariant Wavelets for Quark-Propagator Sparsening and Distillation in Lattice QCD
hep-lat.author: Debsubhra Chakraborty, Nilmani Mathur, Mrinmoy Basak
hep-lat.abstract: We develop a novel gauge-covariant wavelet framework for computing hadronic correlation functions in lattice QCD. Two complementary approaches connect spatial localization and resolution-scale separation to propagator sparsening and distillation. A gauge-covariant fast wavelet transform, based on compactly supported biorthogonal filters, coarse-grains quark propagators and reduces early-time excited-state contamination relative to direct decimation at equal spatial reduction. A second construction applies a resolvent filter of the spatial covariant Laplacian to localized sources, generating a distillation subspace without computing Laplacian eigenpairs. We detail its gauge covariance, smearing profiles, and implementation in exact and stochastic distillation. Spatial localization enables unbiased Hansen-Hurwitz sampling of hadronic contractions, reducing their computational cost substantially. We also examine momentum aliasing induced by fixed coarse grids and the use of random grid shifts to remove unwanted contributions in expectation. Numerical benchmarks of the proposed methods are performed with single hadrons, the I = 2 two-pion system, the deuteron channel, and boosted nucleons. The extracted energy levels agree very well with full or conventional distillation calculations within statistical uncertainties. We quantify the costs of on-demand basis construction and contractions, demonstrate contraction speedups at comparable statistical precision. These studies establish a practical foundation of wavelet-based propagator compression and operator construction for multi-operator calculations of hadronic and nuclear systems, particularly at larger lattice volumes.

hep-lat.title: Two-nucleon scattering amplitudes at light quark masses from lattice QCD
hep-lat.author: Jorge Baeza-Ballesteros, André Baião-Raposo, Davide Laudicina, Malcolm Lazarow, Miguel Salg, John Bulava, Jeremy R. Green, Andrew Hanlon, Renwick J. Hudspith, Daniel Mohler, Colin Morningstar, Amy Nicholson, Fernando Romero-López, Thomas R. Richardson, André Walker-Loud, Hartmut Wittig, for theBaryon Scattering(BaSc)Collaboration
hep-lat.abstract: We present a lattice-QCD determination of nucleon-nucleon scattering amplitudes at pion masses of $M_\pi \approx 200$ MeV and $M_\pi \approx 280$ MeV at a single lattice spacing $a \approx 0.064$ fm on two CLS ensembles. The finite-volume energy spectra are extracted from large Hermitian correlation matrices constructed within the distillation framework using an extensive basis of two-nucleon interpolating operators. To reliably relate the finite-volume spectra to the infinite-volume scattering amplitudes, we employ two recently developed formalisms that explicitly account for the long-range interaction generated by one-pion exchange: the plane-wave quantization condition and the relativistic left-hand-cut formalism. We discuss the quark-mass dependence of the nucleon-nucleon scattering lengths, effective ranges, shape parameters and pole positions. At all pion masses considered, our analysis prefers virtual states in both isospin channels by more than $1\sigma$. Comparing also results from our previous calculation at $M_\pi \approx 710$ MeV, we observe that the inverse scattering lengths and binding momenta approach their physical-point phenomenological values monotonically as the pion mass is varied.

hep-lat.title: Impact of Irrep Truncations on Quantum Simulations of QCD
hep-lat.author: Patrick Draper, Drishti Gupta
hep-lat.abstract: Quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories with continuous gauge groups require a choice of basis (how states of the gauge theory map to the qubit computational basis) and truncation scheme (which of the infinitely many gauge theory basis states should be omitted in the map to the finite dimensional qubit Hilbert space.) The most common choices are adapted to an electric basis for the gauge theory, where the basis states for each link are associated with irreducible representations of the gauge group. Electric bases and truncations are generally advantageous for preserving gauge symmetries and simulating the strong coupling regime, but their effectiveness in the weak coupling regimes of physical interest are less well understood. In this work, we compute relative probabilities $p(R')/p(R)$ for finding a link in the irreps $R,R'$ in the ground state of SU(3) lattice gauge theory using Euclidean Monte Carlo methods and weak-coupling lattice perturbation theory. The observables that compute these relative probabilities are constructed by introducing seams into an anisotropic lattice, and by a similar construction we are also able to measure relative probabilities of different site singlets (ways that electric flux braids together into a gauge singlet) at each vertex. With these methods we can quantify, for example, the importance of higher electric flux states in the weak coupling ground state. These results directly inform what truncations are needed to accurately capture non-abelian gauge dynamics near the continuum limit.

hep-lat.title: Leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude from scalar and axial-vector diquark correlations
hep-lat.author: B. Almeida-Zamora, L. Albino, C. Mezrag, J. Segovia
hep-lat.abstract: We compute the leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude (PDA) using algebraic representations of the nucleon Faddeev wave function inspired by perturbation-theory integral representations. The PDA is obtained from a light-front projection of the covariant quark--diquark Faddeev amplitude and analysed in terms of its scalar- and axial-vector-diquark components. We derive analytic expressions for the corresponding diquark distribution amplitudes and their contributions to the proton PDA. The resulting distribution is broad and concave, with its maximum $(x_1,x_2,x_3)\approx(0.55,0.20,0.25)$ displaced from the symmetric configuration $(1/3,1/3,1/3)$, which corresponds to the maximum of the perturbative-QCD asymptotic form. Scalar-diquark correlations generate a strong asymmetry in the longitudinal momentum distribution, whereas axial-vector correlations redistribute momentum among the valence quarks and significantly reduce this asymmetry. We calculate low-order Mellin moments and obtain a compact parametrisation of the proton PDA at the hadronic scale, $\mu_0=0.51\,\mathrm{GeV}$. We then perform the leading-order QCD evolution of its normalized shape to $\mu=2\,\mathrm{GeV}$, finding that evolution reduces the momentum asymmetry while preserving a clear imprint of the non-perturbative quark--diquark correlations. The results provide insight into the role of such correlations in shaping the proton light-front structure and furnish non-perturbative input for studies of hard exclusive baryonic processes.

hep-lat.title: Complete $g^6$ pressure of hot Yang-Mills theory
hep-lat.author: Keijo Kajantie, Pablo Navarrete, Risto Paatelainen, Leon Sandbote, York Schröder, Kaapo Seppänen, Aleksi Vuorinen
hep-lat.abstract: We present the full order $g^6$ term in the weak-coupling expansion of the pressure of hot $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Yang-Mills theory, resolving a problem that has remained open for more than two decades. To achieve this, we evaluate nine previously unknown nonfactorizing four-loop sum-integrals using the thermal loop-tree duality method with novel local ultraviolet and infrared subtractions, thereby completing the hard-scale contribution to the pressure for general $\mathrm{SU}(N_c)$. Combining this result with known chromoelectric and chromomagnetic contributions, available for $N_c=3$, we demonstrate the analytic cancellation of infrared divergences originating from different momentum scales and obtain the complete $O(g^6)$ pressure for $\mathrm{SU}(3)$. Our result displays quantitative agreement with data from four-dimensional lattice simulations over a broad range of temperatures, providing a stringent test of the dimensionally reduced effective-field-theory paradigm.
