hep-lat.title: The pressure of the gluon plasma at $\mathcal{O}(g_s^6)$, perturbatively
hep-lat.author: Mikael Chala, Luis Gil, Javier López Miras
hep-lat.abstract: We determine the four-loop hard-scale matching correction to the pressure of the gluon plasma at high temperature. This result completes the long-standing calculation through $\mathcal{O}(g_s^6)$, where $g_s$ is the strong coupling. Our result agrees, within uncertainties, with the value obtained inarXiv:1204.6184by fitting the perturbative series to continuum-extrapolated lattice data, thereby providing the first direct test of the weak-coupling expansion at this order.

hep-lat.title: Sampling the XY model with an attention-based neural network
hep-lat.author: Piotr Białas, Christian D. Morales, Tomasz Stebel, Dawid Zapolski
hep-lat.abstract: We present a transformer-based variational autoregressive network for sampling lattice systems with continuous degrees of freedom and apply it to the two-dimensional XY model near the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition. The architecture is combined with physics-informed ingredients: locality-informed attention and approximate probabilities. The resulting sampler significantly outperforms existing neural samplers. We train the model on lattices up to $96\times96$, verify with a mode-dropping estimator that no parts of the configuration space are missed, and reproduce the energy, magnetization and helicity modulus obtained with the traditional Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm.

hep-lat.title: A Monte Carlo Study of the Dipolar Universality Class in Three Dimensions
hep-lat.author: Akira Matsumoto, Yu Nakayama, Toshiki Onagi, Slava Rychkov
hep-lat.abstract: The dipolar universality class describes the phase transition in 3D ferromagnets with strong dipolar interactions, as first discussed by Aharony and Fisher in the 1970s. While this universality class has been studied theoretically using renormalization group methods, as well as experimentally, little is known about it from Monte Carlo simulations. In this paper, we aim to bridge this gap. We introduce a lattice model that faithfully implements the transverse constraint on the order parameter. We introduce a Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm which involves a combination of local Metropolis updates preserving the constraint, and a global update of the zero mode. We perform simulations on cubic lattices up to volume $48\times 48 \times 48$. We observe a continuous phase transition between the disordered and ordered phases. We obtain estimates of the critical exponent $\nu$ and the critical Binder ratio, and compare them with results from other techniques. We also study whether rotational invariance emerges at the critical point, and discuss the influence of the toroidal geometry on this question.

hep-lat.title: Reassessing the $X(2370)$ in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$ beyond the one-dimensional mass projections
hep-lat.author: Xiang-Kun Dong, Teng Ji, Meike Küßner, Ulf-G. Meißner
hep-lat.abstract: The BESIII Collaboration recently extracted the properties of the $X(2370)$ from a fit to the one-dimensional $K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$ invariant-mass spectrum in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$. The intermediate two-body structures visible in the mass correlations, including the $K_0^*(1430)$ bands, require a coherent treatment of cross-channel interference when interpreting the enhancement near 2.3 GeV. We reassess the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution by fitting the published data using an effective coupled-channel framework with an approximate detection efficiency depending on the three-body invariant mass. The three-body parent amplitude is parameterized using a $K$-matrix that describes scattering among several quasi-two-body channels. The seven- and eight-bare-state models give similar mass distributions. Adding the eighth bare state lowers the Poisson deviance by 1.22% and produces an additional pole at $E=(2419-i152)$ MeV, substantially broader than the $X(2370)$ mass-width reference. This pole is model-dependent, and its identification with the $X(2370)$ is not clear. The present analysis does not establish the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$, thereby weakening the flavor-singlet argument based on the suppression of $K^*\bar K$ relative to the total $K\bar K\pi$ contribution. A more comprehensive experimental amplitude analysis, incorporating coherent interference, mass and angular correlations, and detector effects across related decay channels, is needed to establish the role and decay properties of the $X(2370)$.

hep-th.title: Dilaton-Axion Wormhole Partition Function Away from the BPS Endpoint
hep-th.author: Soo-Jong Rey
hep-th.abstract: I determine the leading finite-radius correction to the two-boundary response of a charged axion wormhole near its BPS endpoint. With $\delta=a_*^2$, exact radial matching in a product axion--dilaton/saxion system gives a boundary eigenvalue that vanishes as $O(\delta)$ and an off-diagonal Hessian entry of order $O(\delta^2)$. Their combination produces a cross-boundary covariance linear in $\delta$, with a negative first sub-leading correction on the branch studied here. I determine the semiclassical range in which the quadratic approximation remains controlled and identify the first finite-radius angular resonance, $\delta^2\log(\delta/\delta_0)$. Under a uniform rescaling of all active charges, the coefficient of the linear cross-boundary response scales as the inverse square of the charge scale. I then average the inverse response over the chiral Gaussian ensemble describing the BPS endpoint. Boundary reduction preserves the hard-edge index. Multiplication by the matched BPS sector weight converts the normalized response into the leading finite-radius two-source coefficient.

hep-th.title: A non-prompt null ray cures its own singularity
hep-th.author: Gauri Batra
hep-th.abstract: In AdS/CFT correlators, bulk cone singularities arise when two points that are timelike separated on the AdS boundary may be connected by a null geodesic through the bulk. We consider corrections to these correlators away from the $G_N\to 0$ limit arising from the backreaction of this null geodesic. A peculiar property of this geodesic is that it is not prompt, meaning that there exist points on it that are timelike separated. This implies that it may gravitationally affect itself. We show that this leads to an energy-dependent delay in the time elapsed along this geodesic. This coupled with possible inelastic effects due to gravitational radiation are the leading mechanisms that resolve the singularity. The resolved singularity is accompanied by oscillations and hence zeroes in the real and imaginary parts of the correlator. We comment on the role that additional inelastic effects play in damping these oscillations. Finally, we provide a concrete example in $2+1$D where we can compute the energy-dependent time delay effect explicitly by studying the boundary graviton mode.

hep-th.title: Topological Aspects of the $c=2$ Model in the Continuum and on the Lattice
hep-th.author: Yichul Choi, Nathan Seiberg, Sahand Seifnashri, Wucheng Zhang
hep-th.abstract: We discuss the continuum two-dimensional conformal field theory, whose target space is a two-torus. In addition to its standard zero-form internal symmetries, the model also has a $-1$-form symmetry associated with its $\theta$-parameter, which is also known as a background $B$-field. These symmetries combine into a higher group with anomalies. A spatially winding $B$-field generically breaks the spatial translation symmetry completely, and reduces the continuous target-space (internal) momentum symmetry to a (projectively realized) discrete subgroup. When $B$ varies linearly, a discrete translation subgroup survives, and it combines with the internal symmetry into a non-Abelian group, while the other translations survive as non-invertible symmetries. Even though the model lacks the standard spatial translation symmetry, the non-invertible translation symmetry explains why it is solvable via a Fourier decomposition. We then consider a lattice version of this system, using its modified Villain formulation. Surprisingly, all these subtleties in the symmetries of the continuum model exist on a finite lattice. Finally, we discuss various generalizations of this model, demonstrating that the phenomena we uncovered are more broadly valid.

hep-th.title: Superstring theory in $AdS_5\times S^5$ background: half-BPS vertex operators
hep-th.author: Thiago Fleury, Lucas N. S. Martins, Dennis Zavaleta
hep-th.abstract: In this paper, we construct all vertex operators associated with the gravity supermultiplet in the $AdS_5 \times S^5$ background, relevant for worldsheet scattering amplitude computations, via global $PSU(2,2|4)$ transformations. Although one such operator was previously constructed in the pure spinor formalism using a special superspace parametrization, implementing the full global symmetries proved challenging due to the mixing of bosonic and fermionic coordinates. We resolve this issue by introducing a judicious sequence of reparametrizations that disentangle these coordinates. We then advance the formulation of superstring theory in this background by constructing the corresponding integrated vertex operators in both the pure spinor and the B-RNS-GSS formalisms.

hep-th.title: No cosmic horizons from a strengthened higher-dimensional strong energy condition
hep-th.author: Flavio Tonioni
hep-th.abstract: Time-dependent supergravity compactifications lie beyond the setting of the Gibbons/Maldacena-Nuñez no-de Sitter theorem and can even support eternal cosmic acceleration, raising the question of whether they can also produce future cosmic horizons. For general higher-dimensional matter, the strong energy condition alone does not exclude such horizons. Here, we demonstrate that a theory fulfilling a strengthened version of the strong energy condition cannot be compactified down to a lower-dimensional theory able to support a future cosmic horizon. For 10d and 11d supergravities reduced to at least four large spacetime dimensions, this energy condition is fulfilled by the sources that already fulfill the strong energy condition in the higher-dimensional theory. Our assumption on the dimensional reduction is that it is performed on a smooth compact and boundaryless space.

hep-th.title: Perturbative Defect CFT Data in Scalar Models and Consistency Conditions
hep-th.author: Ziwen Kong
hep-th.abstract: We compute defect CFT data through $O(\epsilon)$ for scalar line defects in the $O(N)$, hypercubic, hypertetrahedral, $O(m)\times O(n)$ biconical, and $MN$ models in $d=4-\epsilon$. The $O(N)$ theory provides a benchmark; the datasets for the other four models are new. For the branches considered, we determine spectra, operator mixing, two- and three-point coefficients in a specified perturbative basis, and four-point functions with identical or paired external operators of integer dimension $n\leq2$ at $\epsilon=0$. We propose a framework for verifying perturbative defect CFT data by combining crossing symmetry, OPE reconstruction, and the applicable broken-symmetry integral identities. We also identify a new universal defect-direction sector whose one-loop data follow from the defect fixed-point equation. All applicable conditions are satisfied at the perturbative orders considered. The model data are collected in the supplemental notebook,this http URL.

hep-th.title: Maximizing the spectral gap for free bosonic CFTs
hep-th.author: Hyeongjoe Chu, Yuchan Jung
hep-th.abstract: We study the spectral gap $\Delta_1$ of Narain CFTs, the smallest scaling dimension of a nonvacuum $U(1)^c_L\times U(1)^c_R$ primary, as a function on the Narain moduli space. Using the exceptional isomorphisms for $SO^+(2,2)$ and $SO^+(3,3)$, we prove the sharp bounds $\Delta_1\le 2/3$ at $c=2$ and $\Delta_1\le 3/4$ at $c=3$, with equality exactly at the $SU(3)_1$ and $SU(4)_1$ WZW models up to $O(c)\times O(c)$, and we describe local maxima of $\Delta_1$. For $4\le c\le 12$, we compare the Narain moduli space with the densest known Euclidean lattices: an arithmetic obstruction excludes five candidates, a computer-assisted classification shows that $E_8$, $K_{12}$, and $BW_{16}$ each admit a unique Narain structure up to lattice automorphisms, and a conceptual argument excludes the Leech lattice.

hep-th.title: Hidden Supersymmetry in AdS/QCD models for Fermions
hep-th.author: Rafael A. Costa-Silva, Henrique Boschi-Filho
hep-th.abstract: We show that the chiral modes splitted from the Dirac equation satisfying Schrodinger-like equations in the context of deformed AdS/QCD model are isospectral, since the chiral effective potentials are SUSY partners. In particular, we show how to perform truncations of these potentials that preserve isospectrality of the chiral modes. Following this prescription, we compare a quadratic approximation of the deformed AdS model with the dressed soft wall model for fermions and show how the spectra of both models can coincide.

hep-th.title: Asymmetric multiscalar fixed points from equiangular tight frames
hep-th.author: Christopher Beem
hep-th.abstract: In their work on multiscalar RG flows, Rychkov and Stergiou posed the question of whether there exist real fixed points of the one-loop renormalization group for scalar field theories in $d=4-\epsilon$ which respect no extra symmetry beyond the universal $\mathbb{Z}_2$ field inversion. In this note, we report on a construction of a large number of such fixed points in the theory of $22001$ scalar fields, thus resolving the question. The construction uses the geometry of an equiangular tight frame in order to reduce the (up to two-loop) fixed point equation to a two-dimensional space of couplings without assuming any extra symmetry. The main technical hurdle is then to establish the existence of such a frame whose corresponding lines preserve no symmetry. This can be achieved using the Steiner frame construction of Fickus, Mixon, and Tremain.

hep-th.title: Optical conductivity of holographic striped superconductors
hep-th.author: Fang-jing Cheng, Kai Li, Yi Ling, Meng-He Wu
hep-th.abstract: Based on a holographic model exhibiting Mott-like insulating behavior on an ionic lattice, we construct a holographic striped superconductor (SSC), which is characterized by the interplay between the charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity (SC). We present the phase diagram on the $e$-$T$ plane, where the SSC phase emerges within an intermediate window of $e$, revealing both cooperative and competitive relations between the CDW order and SC order. For small charge $e$, the system undergoes the phase transition from metallic phase to CDW phase, and then to SSC phase upon cooling; while for large $e$, it transitions from metallic phase to SC phase directly, and then to SSC phase. We compute the optical conductivity of the system for these two cases and demonstrate its distinct behavior. It turns out that the imaginary part of the conductivity exhibits a divergent behavior below the critical temperature $T_{\mathrm{SSC}}$ along both pathways, so that the superconductivity of SSC phase is justified for the first time in the holographic framework. Along the CDW-to-SSC pathway the pseudogap and the pinning effect are inherited from the CDW phase, whereas along the SC-to-SSC pathway the spontaneous stripe strongly suppresses the coherent normal-fluid channel while the superfluid pole is enhanced. In addition, we demonstrate the commensurate lock-in behavior of the striped superconductor in the $p$-$T$ diagram.

hep-th.title: Exact $T\bar{T}$-Like Flows in Nonlinear Electrodynamics
hep-th.author: Zahra Pezhman, H. Babaei-Aghbolagh, Komeil Babaei Velni
hep-th.abstract: We derive an exact nonperturbative $T\bar T$-like flow for the class of one-scale, self-dual nonlinear electrodynamics theories admitting a Courant--Hilbert representation. The flow has a universal parametric form in terms of the defining Courant--Hilbert function and, on any physical branch where the relevant invariant map is invertible, becomes an autonomous function of the two quadratic stress-tensor invariants, $\partial_\lambda\mathcal L=X\,\mathcal F(Y/X)$. The function $\mathcal F$ is model dependent, and global autonomy is assumed when the invariant map is one-to-one. Born--Infeld theory yields a quadratic stress-tensor flow, whereas the causal Russo--Townsend logarithmic model gives an exact nonlinear expression involving the Lambert $W$ function whose weak-field expansion reproduces the known perturbative result. We also establish the equivalence with the Russo--Townsend auxiliary-field formulation. These results provide an exact construction of autonomous irrelevant flows for a broad, explicitly specified class of self-dual nonlinear electrodynamics theories.

hep-th.title: Scalar Casimir Effect from Bilocal Correlations in a Wormhole Foam
hep-th.author: Celio R. Muniz, M. C. Araújo, Edson Otoniel, Jonathan A. Rebouças
hep-th.abstract: We determine how spatially bilocal correlations induced by a dilute ensemble of virtual Euclidean wormholes modify the scalar Casimir interaction between parallel Dirichlet plates. From the leading monopole action, we isolate an equal-Euclidean-time sector and construct a point-throat, first-order matched spectator model with fixed foam statistics. Global two-plate inclusion-exclusion over all mouth-pair center positions yields a continuous fixed-separation kernel free of the logarithmic image structures produced by a restricted translation sector. The kernel is quadratically suppressed at coincidence, changes sign near 0.695 plate spacings, and tends to a positive large-separation plateau. Averaging over truncated-Gaussian, log-normal, and Gamma distributions with a common relative width yields closely spaced energy curves but a finite shape dependence. Differentiating the dimensional energy at fixed ensemble parameters gives a leading-order pressure threshold of 0.05 in the large-separation limit. In the truncated-Gaussian scan extending to twelve plate spacings, an amplitude of 0.06 yields a crossover near a separation ratio of 3.17, whereas amplitudes of 0.02 and 0.04 remain attractive and 0.05 is critical. The scalar cavity therefore provides a scale-selective probe of spatial bilocality whose leading boundary response can change sign within the declared model.

hep-th.title: Spinors, Doppelgängers and the Non-Perturbative Classical Double Copy
hep-th.author: Kymani Armstrong-Williams
hep-th.abstract: We develop a geometric and spinorial formulation of the non-perturbative classical double copy between the Corrigan--Fairlie--'t Hooft--Wilczek sector of complexified SU(2) Yang--Mills theory and four-dimensional conformally flat gravity. We identify the gauge potential with the positive-chiral spin connection of the conformally flat metric, establishing an exact relation between the Yang--Mills field strength and the chiral projection of the Riemann tensor. This provides a four-dimensional realisation of the doppelgänger viewpoint, in which gauge and gravitational fields arise from different interpretations of common connection data. Within this sector, the sourceless Yang--Mills equations require constant scalar curvature, explaining the shared nonlinear scalar equation and extending the gravitational correspondence from traceless matter to matter with constant energy--momentum trace. By representing adjoint colour indices as symmetric pairs of spinor indices, we derive exact relations mapping the gauge field-strength spinors to the scalar-curvature and trace-free Ricci components of the gravitational curvature. These relations retain nontrivial curvature information despite the vanishing Weyl tensor. We illustrate the construction using anti-de Sitter and de Sitter spacetimes, together with $\mathrm{AdS}_{3}\times\mathbb{R}$ supported by a scalar field, demonstrating the extension to matter with nonzero constant trace

hep-th.title: Compensator-free $\mathcal N=2$ extension of ModMax and scalar propagation
hep-th.author: Ariunzul Davgadorj
hep-th.abstract: We construct a compensator-free $\mathcal N=2$ superconformal and electric--magnetic duality-invariant extension of ModMax electrodynamics in ordinary flat superspace. The action is built entirely from the Abelian vector multiplet, using a derivative composite of its field strength, and the self-duality equation is solved to all orders as a formal series in the coupling. Upon setting the additional $\mathcal N=1$ chiral multiplet to zero, the action is equivalent off shell to the $\mathcal N=1$ ModMax action of Bandos, Lechner, Sorokin and Townsend through a local vector-prepotential redefinition.Since the complex scalar of the $\mathcal N=2$ multiplet is set to zero in this reduction, we add one superconformal interaction that leaves the reduction unchanged and is chosen to ensure causal scalar propagation. On constant non-null electromagnetic backgrounds with vanishing scalar expectation value, the higher-order scalar coefficients are fixed by requiring the scalar quadratic action to satisfy the stress-tensor square-root flow, modulo equations of motion and a total derivative. We determine the quadratic action of the full multiplet on these backgrounds to all orders. Its analytic continuation to finite $\gamma\geq0$ gives causal scalar propagation, with transverse speed squared $e^{-\gamma}$ and unit longitudinal speed, the ModMax photon cones, luminal gauginos with positive kinetic coefficients, and auxiliary fields with algebraic equations of motion.

hep-th.title: When Conformal Interfaces Become Logarithmic
hep-th.author: Jin Chen
hep-th.abstract: We construct conformal interfaces having defect conformal manifolds between two-dimensional rational CFTs, at least one of which is non-unitary. In a continuous family, interfaces with real and complex spectra can be marginally deformed to each other via their defect moduli parameters. An exceptional point then arises along the trajectory in the conformal manifold, where two interface operators with complex conjugate weights coalesce into a logarithmic pair. We reconstruct the entire trajectory of this novel spectral collision, independently, from self-annulus partition functions and bulk two point correlators in the presence of the interfaces.

hep-th.title: Timelike entanglement entropy with gravitational anomaly from complexified geometry
hep-th.author: Minwoo Lim, Himanshu Parihar, Junggi Yoon
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the timelike entanglement entropy (TEE) in a two-dimensional conformal field theory with a gravitational anomaly, $c_L\neq c_R$, dual to topologically massive gravity in AdS$_3$. Holographically, the TEE is determined by the on-shell action of a massive spinning particle on a single complex geodesic anchored at the endpoints of the timelike interval. This action consists of the complex geodesic length and the twist of a parallel-transported normal frame. We carry out the computation in Poincaré AdS$_3$, non-extremal and extremal rotating BTZ backgrounds, and provide an equivalent Chern-Simons derivation in which the bulk connection stays real while only the saddle of the Wilson-line probe becomes complex. In each case, the holographic result matches the corresponding TEE in dual field theory. The real part of the TEE is fixed unambiguously whereas its imaginary part depends on the boundary $i\epsilon$ prescription and the orientation of the interval. In the bulk, the dependence on orientation reflects an ambiguity in the choice of framing. Along the complex geodesic, the residual frame group becomes $SO(2,\mathbb C)\simeq\mathbb C^*$, so the endpoint conditions determine the frame twist only up to integer multiples of $2\pi i$. The difference between the two orientations, $\frac{c_L-c_R}{6}\,i\pi$, is fixed entirely by the gravitational anomaly and persists for the Rényi pseudo-entropies.

hep-th.title: Renormalization Group Domain Walls from Phantom Symmetries
hep-th.author: Jin Chen
hep-th.abstract: We develop a systematic construction of renormalization group (RG) domain walls between two-dimensional rational conformal field theories. Using phantom currents, we consider an auxiliary chiral extension linked to the folded ultraviolet--infrared theory by a topological interface. The construction of RG walls then reduces to identifying suitable automorphism-twisted Cardy states in the auxiliary theory. We find two such types of automorphisms: outer automorphisms exchanging identical current algebra factors, as in Gaiotto's construction, and continuous inner automorphisms generated by the zero modes of spin-one phantom currents. In the latter case, the RG domain walls generically admit a continuous defect conformal manifold. We further show that, when an RG flow can be orbifolded to another one, the orbifold may lift defect conformal moduli of the RG brane constructed using inner automorphisms. The two types of RG branes can then be mapped to each other via a topological interface defined by the orbifold. We demonstrate the two types of RG brane construction via various examples of flows between non-unitary minimal models, from parafermions to minimal models, and between generalized parafermions. Many physical observables of the RG walls are computed non-perturbatively, including boundary entropies and spectra, and UV--IR operator mixings. We also find interesting nontrivial boundary monodromy: a closed cycle in the defect conformal moduli space can carry an RG domain wall into other distinct non-trivial conformal interfaces.

hep-th.title: Holographic two-point functions across a PT symmetry-breaking transition
hep-th.author: Zuo Wang, Liang He
hep-th.abstract: In parity-time (PT)-symmetric non-Hermitian systems, an exceptional point, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, typically separates a real spectrum from complex-conjugate eigenvalues. In logarithmic conformal field theories (LCFTs), such an exceptional point appears in the spectrum of scaling dimensions. Holographic models of LCFTs, such as the dipole model, are built exactly at this point. Here, we deform the holographic dipole model so that its two coalescing scaling dimensions split into either two real ones or a complex-conjugate pair. We obtain the renormalized two-point functions in closed form. They change continuously from a linear combination of two power laws, through the logarithmic form of the LCFT at the exceptional point, to log-periodic oscillations. For any pair of scalar primary operators with real mixing under dilatations, the conformal Ward identities fix this form up to two normalization constants, which the holographic dictionary determines. In PT-symmetric theories with such a dilatation operator, real and complex-conjugate scaling dimensions correspond to the PT-unbroken and PT-broken phases. In the BTZ black hole at finite temperature, the difference between the quasinormal frequencies associated with the two scaling dimensions changes from purely imaginary to purely real across the real-to-complex spectral transition. Correspondingly, the linear response changes from overdamped to underdamped, with critical damping at the exceptional point.

hep-th.title: Runaways in the no-boundary wavefunction
hep-th.author: Jordan Cotler, Prateksh Dhivakar, William Harvey, Victor Ivo, Kristan Jensen
hep-th.abstract: We study the no-boundary wavefunction of Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant. We identify families of weakly curved bulk saddles, including fillings of anisotropic late-time universes $\mathbb{S}^p\times\mathbb{S}^q$, whose weights grow exponentially with geometric parameters of the late-time boundary. These runaways threaten the normalizability of the no-boundary state within gravitational effective field theory. Whether these saddles contribute remains open. Many of the runaway families we study violate the Kontsevich-Segal-Witten criterion, although several are minus asymptotically hyperbolic geometries whose one-loop determinants appear well-defined for pure gravity. For $\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^q$ universes with $q\equiv 0\pmod4$, we construct a contour integral model that excludes the runaway at large $\mathbb{S}^q$.

hep-th.title: A Levinson's theorem for particle form factors
hep-th.author: Francesco Rosini, Simone Pacetti
hep-th.abstract: We present and demonstrate a version of Levinson's theorem especially dedicated to the asymptotic behavior of form factor phases. Indeed, as required by analyticity, form factors are multi-valued complex functions of a square four-momentum defined in the complex plane with a cut along the positive real axis. Their phases evaluated on the upper edge of this cut, i.e., on the time-like region, tend asymptotically to integer multiples of $\pi$ radians. The Levinson's theorem establishes a univocal relation between such multiples and properties of form factors related to the dynamics of the electromagnetic interaction of the corresponding hadrons.

hep-th.title: Noise-Induced Restoration of Entropy Concavity Near Gaussian Equilibrium
hep-th.author: Fayez Abu-Ajamieh
hep-th.abstract: We study a quantitative form of noise-induced restoration of entropy concavity for one-dimensional nonequilibrium states relaxing toward a Gaussian thermal equilibrium. A partially thermalized state is modeled by $X_q=\sqrt q\,X+\sqrt{1-q}\,G$, where $G$ is Gaussian equilibrium noise and $q$ is the retained signal fraction. For two independently prepared copies we ask when the entropy of the mixed state $h(\sqrt{1-t}\,X_q+\sqrt t\,Y_q)$ is concave in the mixing parameter. The problem is motivated by entropy geometry along Ornstein--Uhlenbeck/Fokker--Planck relaxation, where the relative score is the nonequilibrium thermodynamic force and relative Fisher information is entropy-production rate. We derive an exact symmetric endpoint-curvature formula, separating a nonnegative Ornstein--Uhlenbeck restoring term from a fourth-cumulant correction, and extend it to nonsmooth generalized-Gaussian states $e^{-a|x|^p}$ for $p>3/2$. For half thermalization of a symmetric log-concave input, posterior-variance identities give a quantitative outer-region theorem confining any endpoint obstruction to two explicitly bounded near-equilibrium sectors. We also give spectral and MMSE reformulations of the auxiliary inequality $A\ge2\delta$, prove it in an explicit nonlinear neighborhood of Gaussian equilibrium, and show how it sharpens the endpoint bounds. The main all-mixing result concerns the leading symmetric non-Gaussian Hermite mode: for $p_a=\phiG(1+a\He_4)$, $0<a\le10^{-2}$, we prove strict entropy concavity for every $0<t<1$ and every $0<q\le5/8$, hence throughout the currently unresolved symmetric range $0<q\le4/7$ for this explicit nonequilibrium family. Numerical searches over broader log-concave families are reported only as supporting evidence.

hep-th.title: General Relativity in Three Lines
hep-th.author: Pawel Nurowski
hep-th.abstract: We show that complex general relativity can be formulated directly in terms of three affine lines assigned to each spacetime point. The lines are represented by Plücker bivectors, and Urbantke's construction applied to the associated two-forms reconstructs the conformal spacetime metric. Starting from the chiral Plebański action, the simplicity constraints turn the three two-forms into a null internal basis of simple bivectors and thereby into three projective lines. A $3+1$ decomposition then yields a first-order canonical theory whose configuration variable is the weighted triple of lines and whose conjugate variable is a line momentum. The resulting constraint system consists of three internal Gauss constraints, three vector constraints, and one Hamiltonian constraint.A notable feature of the line formulation is that the equation obtained by varying the line momentum is pointwise algebraic after the spatial integrations by parts. Consequently the momentum can be eliminated explicitly wherever the corresponding Legendre map is invertible, giving a second-order action whose only dynamical configuration variable is the weighted triple of lines. The line curvature separates naturally into a cosmological trace and the Weyl matrix of the selected chiral sector. The Legendre map becomes singular on a distinguished null-evolution locus where the spacetime metric remains nondegenerate. There its rank drops from nine to six, giving three algebraic compatibility conditions. We construct a finite invariant partial Legendre transform and a smooth constrained second-order continuation through this locus. This analysis provides a regular framework for regimes in which the evolution direction becomes null and may be useful in the study of near-horizon geometries and related gravitational phenomena.

hep-th.title: Dynamical entropy and thermodynamics of causal diamonds
hep-th.author: Avik Chakraborty, Pratik K. Das, Manavendra Mahato
hep-th.abstract: We study the dynamical entropy of causal diamonds using Wald-Zoupas charges and fluxes on their null boundaries. For a chosen boundary symplectic potential, the boost charge defines an entropy made of an area term plus an expansion correction, which reduces to one quarter of the area at the edge on the diamond. In Einstein gravity, we find an exact balance law relating the entropy on any two cuts of the null boundary to a signed flux, so the entropy decreases only when this flux is non-negative. We obtain a linearised physical process first law without assuming a background Killing symmetry, both in the presence and absence of external matter; and extend it for semiclassical gravity based on the improved quantum null energy condition. We also examine causal diamonds in maximally symmetric spacetimes and in Einstein-scalar gravity.

hep-th.title: Angular Momenta in $4+1$ Vacuum Critical Collapse
hep-th.author: Oscar J.C. Dias, Carsten Gundlach, Jorge E. Santos, Benson Way
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the critical collapse of gravitational waves that carry angular momenta. Working in five-dimensional vacuum Einstein gravity under an SU$(2)\times\mathbb Z_4$ symmetry ansatz, we numerically evolve several families of initial data near the threshold of black-hole formation. Near-critical data approaches the discretely self-similar Bizoń-Chmaj-Schmidt solution, which is irrotational. We find that the near-threshold mass scaling has a universal critical exponent, but the angular-momentum scaling has one of two critical exponents, depending on the family of initial data. The angular-momentum critical exponents are therefore not universal under this symmetry ansatz. Our results agree with predictions from perturbation theory about the critical solution.

hep-th.title: The Singular Structure of Rapidity Distributions for Color-Singlet Production at N3LO
hep-th.author: Federica Devoto, Bernhard Mistlberger, Gherardo Vita
hep-th.abstract: We determine the universal singular structure of rapidity distributions for color-singlet production in hadron collisions through next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N3LO) in QCD. Our result captures the full singular contributions as either partonic momentum fraction approaches one, including the delta-function terms, while retaining the exact dependence on the other. The essential new ingredient is the complete calculation of the three-loop quark and gluon rapidity beam-function matching kernels. Our calculation is based on the strict collinear expansion of the partonic cross sections for Higgs boson and Drell-Yan production. We represent our results in terms of generalized polylogarithms as well as numerical series expansions. The resulting N3LO partonic coefficient functions apply to arbitrary color-singlet production processes with the process dependence entering through the hard function, which encodes the virtual corrections to the Born process.

hep-th.title: Asymptotic evaluation of multidimensional oscillatory integrals
hep-th.author: Samuel Crew, Job Feldbrugge
hep-th.abstract: Oscillatory integrals appear throughout physics, from diffraction and gravitational lensing to real-time path integrals. Their asymptotic evaluation is complicated by the need to determine which real and complex saddle points contribute, and how they are connected by Stokes phenomena. In multiple dimensions, this traditionally requires computing steepest descent manifolds in a high-dimensional complex space. Here, we develop an algebraic alternative for integrals with polynomial and rational exponents. Using integration by parts and Brieskorn reduction, we construct a finite-dimensional Gauss-Manin system that generates the asymptotic expansion of all saddle points. Its Borel transform yields a Fuchsian system, whose mondromy determines the Stokes constants and hence the adjacency of the saddle points. Combined with the recent South-East rule, this identifies the contributing saddles and enables superasymptotic and hyperasymptotic approximations without computing gradient flows. We demonstate the method for the parabolic umbilic diffraction integral and a Lorentzian lens as examples, obtaining agreement to machine precision. The methods are implemented in an accompanying open-source Julia packagethis http URL

hep-th.title: Environment-induced topological reconstruction of black-hole thermodynamics
hep-th.author: Xinyu Zhou, Chen Lan, Zhen-Ming Xu
hep-th.abstract: Thermodynamic topology describes black-hole (BH) equilibria as zeros, or defects, of a vector field built from the off-shell free energy. Studies with surrounding matter find that the topological class is unchanged, but not how the matter's spatial distribution affects individual equilibria. We ask whether the position of a localized environment can reorganize these equilibria at fixed total topological number. We model the environment as a radially localized energy bump peaked at $a_m$ and add its exterior energy to the generalized off-shell free energy. As $a_m$ varies, defects migrate and are created or annihilated in opposite-charge pairs, a process we call topological reconstruction. It changes the number and stability of equilibrium branches but preserves the total topological number, provided no zero crosses the boundary of the physical domain. We find this in Schwarzschild, Schwarzschild-AdS, Reissner-Nordström, and Reissner-Nordström-AdS BHs, with critical positions and required strength that depend on the background. In our examples, the required environmental energy ranges from below $1\%$ of the BH mass to a value comparable to it. The model is an effective fixed-background description without backreaction. Within it, the total topological number cannot capture the environmental response; local defects must be tracked.

hep-th.title: Universal Long-distance Tail of Particle-number Density near a Wall in Superfluids
hep-th.author: Keisuke Fujii
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the long-distance recovery of the particle-number density near a static, impermeable wall in a $d$-dimensional Galilean-invariant superfluid. Using superfluid effective field theory (EFT) on a half-space, we show that quantum phonon fluctuations produce a $z^{-(d+1)}$ tail in the smooth density profile at zero temperature, where $z$ is the distance from the wall. The tail coefficient is fixed by the bulk equation of state and is independent of microscopic wall details. At low temperature $T$, the thermal length $c_s/T$, with $c_s$ the bulk sound speed, separates the zero-temperature behavior at intermediate distances from a thermal $Tz^{-d}$ tail at larger distances for $d>1$. For $d=1$, the long-distance phonon contribution instead decays as $\exp(-4\pi Tz/c_s)$. The EFT applies to both Bose and Fermi superfluids, including strongly interacting Fermi gases at unitarity. We estimate the normalized tail amplitude in three dimensions across the BCS--BEC crossover using experimental sound-speed data.

hep-th.title: Consistency Checks for Λ positive Quantum Cosmology
hep-th.author: S. P. Miao, N. C. Tsamis, R. P. Woodard
hep-th.abstract: In this paper we improve and further analyze the recently derived quantum gravity equations which apply in accelerating cosmological spacetimes and whose solutions re-sum leading logarithms from all orders of perturbation theory. We show the consistency of these upgraded equations against 1-loop non-trivial exact perturbative computations. The upgraded equations retain their remarkably simple form.

hep-th.title: Gauge-Covariant Wavelets for Quark-Propagator Sparsening and Distillation in Lattice QCD
hep-th.author: Debsubhra Chakraborty, Nilmani Mathur, Mrinmoy Basak
hep-th.abstract: We develop a novel gauge-covariant wavelet framework for computing hadronic correlation functions in lattice QCD. Two complementary approaches connect spatial localization and resolution-scale separation to propagator sparsening and distillation. A gauge-covariant fast wavelet transform, based on compactly supported biorthogonal filters, coarse-grains quark propagators and reduces early-time excited-state contamination relative to direct decimation at equal spatial reduction. A second construction applies a resolvent filter of the spatial covariant Laplacian to localized sources, generating a distillation subspace without computing Laplacian eigenpairs. We detail its gauge covariance, smearing profiles, and implementation in exact and stochastic distillation. Spatial localization enables unbiased Hansen-Hurwitz sampling of hadronic contractions, reducing their computational cost substantially. We also examine momentum aliasing induced by fixed coarse grids and the use of random grid shifts to remove unwanted contributions in expectation. Numerical benchmarks of the proposed methods are performed with single hadrons, the I = 2 two-pion system, the deuteron channel, and boosted nucleons. The extracted energy levels agree very well with full or conventional distillation calculations within statistical uncertainties. We quantify the costs of on-demand basis construction and contractions, demonstrate contraction speedups at comparable statistical precision. These studies establish a practical foundation of wavelet-based propagator compression and operator construction for multi-operator calculations of hadronic and nuclear systems, particularly at larger lattice volumes.

hep-th.title: Anticommuting Displacement Operators, Exact Pauli Algebras,and the Singlet State from the Oscillator Vacuum
hep-th.author: S. P. Sorella
hep-th.abstract: We give an explicit construction of a pair of anticommuting Weyl displacement operators for a harmonic oscillator and use bounded functional calculus to obtain exact dichotomic representatives of the Pauli algebra. Two independent oscillators provide commuting Pauli algebras for Alice and Bob. The standard singlet-sector projector, written entirely in terms of these bounded oscillator observables, is then applied to the two-oscillator vacuum. We show explicitly that the projected vacuum has nonzero norm, so its normalization is well defined, has the exact singlet correlations, and reaches the Tsirelson value $2\sqrt2$ for the usual Bell--CHSH settings. We also clarify that the construction generally realizes a singlet sector with multiplicity, rather than selecting a unique vector in the full oscillator Hilbert space, and we compare the construction with the older pseudospin approach to continuous-variable Bell tests.

hep-th.title: Principle of no paradoxical Universe
hep-th.author: Ngo Phuc Duc Loc
hep-th.abstract: In the standard $\Lambda\rm CDM$ model, the Universe will keep expanding forever and its lifetime is infinite. Therefore, even the heaviest supermassive black hole will eventually evaporate and the universal occurrence of the black hole information paradox is unavoidable. However, the recent DESI results seem to indicate that dark energy is dynamical and, more importantly, it is possible that the Universe has a finite lifetime and will experience a ``Big Crunch" in some billion years from now. In light of this, the lightest confirmed black hole with mass of order one solar mass may not have a chance to evaporate before the Universe ends. Inspired by these observations, we thus raise an intriguing conjecture: Does the Universe choose a configuration such that the ``in-principle" black hole information paradox can never actually happen in reality? We derive a lower bound on black hole mass as a function of the Universe's lifetime such that the information paradox cannot be realized in nature and some resulting predictions are made. Some profound implications for other related big ideas in physics are briefly discussed.

hep-th.title: Complete $g^6$ pressure of hot Yang-Mills theory
hep-th.author: Keijo Kajantie, Pablo Navarrete, Risto Paatelainen, Leon Sandbote, York Schröder, Kaapo Seppänen, Aleksi Vuorinen
hep-th.abstract: We present the full order $g^6$ term in the weak-coupling expansion of the pressure of hot $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Yang-Mills theory, resolving a problem that has remained open for more than two decades. To achieve this, we evaluate nine previously unknown nonfactorizing four-loop sum-integrals using the thermal loop-tree duality method with novel local ultraviolet and infrared subtractions, thereby completing the hard-scale contribution to the pressure for general $\mathrm{SU}(N_c)$. Combining this result with known chromoelectric and chromomagnetic contributions, available for $N_c=3$, we demonstrate the analytic cancellation of infrared divergences originating from different momentum scales and obtain the complete $O(g^6)$ pressure for $\mathrm{SU}(3)$. Our result displays quantitative agreement with data from four-dimensional lattice simulations over a broad range of temperatures, providing a stringent test of the dimensionally reduced effective-field-theory paradigm.

hep-th.title: The pressure of the gluon plasma at $\mathcal{O}(g_s^6)$, perturbatively
hep-th.author: Mikael Chala, Luis Gil, Javier López Miras
hep-th.abstract: We determine the four-loop hard-scale matching correction to the pressure of the gluon plasma at high temperature. This result completes the long-standing calculation through $\mathcal{O}(g_s^6)$, where $g_s$ is the strong coupling. Our result agrees, within uncertainties, with the value obtained inarXiv:1204.6184by fitting the perturbative series to continuum-extrapolated lattice data, thereby providing the first direct test of the weak-coupling expansion at this order.

hep-th.title: Spectral networks, finite webs, and the $T_3$ cubic differential
hep-th.author: Omar Kidwai, Guillaume Tahar
hep-th.abstract: We describe spectral networks for cubic differentials on $\mathbf{P}^1$ with exactly three poles all of order two, following observations of Hollands-Neitzke. To do so, we give a precise definition and establish some basic properties of a class of finite webs (corresponding to BPS states in physics) in the cubic differential setting, including their non-vanishing central charge. Turning to the example, we prove that at rational angles the network is totally degenerate; the number of walls and Stokes regions is explicitly computed and depends on an arithmetic criterion. At all other angles, the spectral network is dense in the surface and contains no finite webs, as expected. Physically, this example corresponds to a fundamental building block for a large class of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ QFTs with gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(3)$.

hep-th.title: Anyonic Neural Network Wavefunctions
hep-th.author: Andres Perez Fadon, Pok Man Tam, Leyna Shackleton
hep-th.abstract: The macroscopic behavior of a non-interacting gas of Abelian anyons has remained unsettled for many decades. Prior numerical methods employing exact diagonalization in the continuum and on the plane have been limited to small system sizes, at most $N = 4$ anyons. Using the rapidly developing technology of neural network wavefunctions, we develop variational ansatze appropriate for studying continuum models of the Abelian anyon gas. The neural network architecture, which we call "AnyNet", is capable of exactly enforcing the non-analytic short-distance behavior induced by the anyonic statistics. We demonstrate excellent agreement with exact diagonalization for $N=4$ anyons, obtain accurate results up to $N = 16$ for intermediate statistics, and study up to $N=20$ for almost-fermionic anyons, matching perturbative results within a 0.4% discrepancy. We use this methodology to study anyons in a harmonic trap, and anyonic atoms as a model for anyon binding to impurities. We study the structure of anyonic wavefunctions as the statistics parameter is varied. We focus on the single-particle density, the pair density, the angular momentum, and the scaling of the wavefunction as multiple anyons coalesce. This work opens doors to understanding the macroscopic behavior of anyons, for which rich phases have been predicted theoretically.

hep-th.title: Graded transcendental functions: an application to four-point amplitudes with one off-shell leg
hep-th.author: Thomas Gehrmann, Johannes Henn, Petr Jakubčík, Jungwon Lim, Cesare Carlo Mella, Nikolaos Syrrakos, Lorenzo Tancredi, William J. Torres Bobadilla
hep-th.abstract: Several recent works have demonstrated the powerful algebraic simplifications that can be achieved for scattering amplitudes through a systematic grading of transcendental quantities. We develop these concepts to construct a minimal basis of functions tailored to a scattering amplitude in a general way. Starting with formal solutions for all master integral topologies, we organise the appearing functions by properties such as their symbol alphabet or letter adjacency. We rotate the basis such that functions with spurious features appear in the least possible number of basis elements. Since their coefficients must vanish for physical quantities, this approach avoids complex cancellations. As a first application, we evaluate all integral topologies relevant to the three-loop $Hggg$ and $Hgq\bar{q}$ amplitudes in the leading-colour approximation and heavy-top limit. We describe the derivation of canonical differential equation systems and present a method for fixing boundary conditions without the need for a full functional representation. Using multiple numerical reductions, we test the maximal transcendentality conjecture for $Hggg$ and identify a new letter which appears in functions of weight 4 and 5. In addition, we provide the first direct analytic computation of a three-point form factor of the operator $\mathrm{Tr}(\phi^2)$ in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ sYM and find agreement with numerical and bootstrapped results.

hep-th.title: Holographic entanglement entropy and c-functions in conformal and confining backgrounds
hep-th.author: Jonathan Whittle
hep-th.abstract: In this work we investigate holographic spacelike and timelike entanglement entropy using the Ryu-Takayanagi prescription, for slab-shaped and ball-shaped entangling regions. We work with an infinite family of 10-dimensional Type IIB supergravity solutions, which are gravity duals to an infinite set of linear quiver theories, with the backgrounds defined using the electrostatic potential formalism for brane configurations. The dual theories are 4-dimensional confining theories at low energy, but decompactify and flow to 5-dimensional SCFTs in the UV. We find that the entanglement entropy exhibits phase transition behaviour, and we use our results to investigate proposed c-functions constructed from the entanglement entropy. Comparing with the flow central charge, another proposed c-function, we find that each displays good behaviour, and reflects both UV and IR features of the dual theory.

hep-th.title: Fluid dynamics as intersection problem
hep-th.author: Nikita Nekrasov, Paul Wiegmann
hep-th.abstract: The main result of the paper is a construction of an infinite-dimensional symplectic manifold, associated with spacetime, its coisotropic submanifold defined as the zero locus of a moment map, and a family of Lagrangian submanifolds determined by the equation of state and the spacetime metric, such that their intersection is precisely the covariant Lichnerowicz--Carter system for a relativistic perfect fluid. On this basis, we clarify the notion of canonical velocity and hydrodynamic invariants, such as the asymptotic Hopf invariant and the Ertel invariant, and obtain a generalization of Kelvin's circulation theorem. We also clarify the relation between the canonical velocity, the four-velocity, and other choices of frames. We point out a five-dimensional origin of the formalism underlying the covariant formulation of hydrodynamics.Our formalism extends naturally to fluids with additional degrees of freedom, including multi-component fluids, charged fluids, and superfluids, and incorporates the chiral anomaly and Onsager quantization. It also suggests a direction of research connecting hydrodynamics to Poisson sigma models and topological field theories.Furthermore, we argue that a similar approach applies to the theory of self-dual fields, such as chiral bosons in 1+1 dimensions, tensor fields of (2,0) theory in 1+5 dimensions, and the 4-form field of type-IIB supergravity in 1+9 dimensions.

hep-th.title: D-instanton Effects on the Holographic Weyl Semimetals
hep-th.author: Hwajin Eom, Yunseok Seo
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the effects of D-instantons on a holographic Weyl semimetal in a top-down approach. We find that the presence of D-instantons induces a novel phase transition from a Weyl semimetal to a gapped phase, providing a new mechanism for gap formation in strongly coupled systems. By analyzing the free energy of probe D7-brane embeddings, we construct the phase diagram in terms of the fermion mass, instanton density, and temperature, measured in units of the Weyl parameter. We show that, in addition to the conventional mass-driven transition associated with band inversion, the instanton density gives rise to a qualitatively different transition whose mechanism cannot be understood within the standard Dirac picture. We compute nonlinear electric conductivities from the regularity condition at the black hole horizon and demonstrate that the two types of transitions exhibit distinct transport behavior. In particular, the instanton-induced transition leads to a gapped phase with properties that differ from the conventional insulating phase. We also discuss possible interpretations of this phase in the boundary theory and comment on its relation to nonperturbative effects in strongly interacting systems.

hep-th.title: IR behaviour of one-loop complex $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$ saddles
hep-th.author: Shubhashis Mallik, Gaurav Narain
hep-th.abstract: Gravitational path-integral over $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$ complex metrics with fluctuations is studied in 4D for Einstein-Hilbert gravity in Lorentzian signature, with the aim to investigate the IR behaviour of complex saddles for various boundary choices. General covariance doesn't allow arbitrary boundary choices for the background and fluctuations. In the ADM-decomposition, while imposing ``no-boundary'' condition at the initial boundary, two scenarios are considered for the final boundary: Dirichlet and fixed extrinsic curvature. The universe undergoes a transition from a Euclidean to a Lorentzian phase in either scenario, where the dominant saddle in Euclidean phase corresponds to a Euclidean metric, while the Lorentzian phase has two dominant complex saddles that superimpose. One-loop lapse action is computed using Hurwitz-Zeta regularization. UV-divergences canceled by suitable counterterms lead to a renormalized lapse action. One-loop Hartle-Hawking wave-function is computed using the Picard-Lefschetz (PL) and WKB methods, where the contributions from the metric fluctuations show secularly growing infrared divergences as the Universe expands. This is compared with the situation in Lorentzian dS, corresponding to a Universe transitioning from an initial state of vanishing conjugate momenta to a final state of fixed extrinsic curvature. The PL method alone is not sufficient to overcome the technical hurdles in the one-loop computation, which needs to be supplemented by an $i\epsilon$-prescription, achieved via slight complexification of the cosmological constant $\Lambda$. The renormalized one-loop dS wavefunction is seen to have qualitatively the same leading IR behaviour as the no-boundary wavefunction, though the coefficients are seen to be sensitive to the UV boundary choices. Interestingly, for all boundary choices considered, the saddles remain KSW-allowed.

hep-th.title: Kerr/CFT Traversable Wormhole with Fermionic Double-Trace Deformation
hep-th.author: M. Zhahir Djogama, Fitria Khairunnisa, Hadyan Luthfan Prihadi, Freddy Permana Zen
hep-th.abstract: The construction of a traversable wormhole with double-trace deformation has been achieved so far by using boson fields as the perturbation. In this work, we study double-trace deformation with fermion fields in the two-sided Kerr background to open a traversable wormhole. We construct the fermionic double-trace deformation within the Kerr/CFT framework. We consider the near-horizon, near-extremal Kerr geometry, which is dual to a conformal field theory. The lack of fermionic superradiance let us describe the wormhole at every region, even at the off-axis region where bosonic field experiences instability due to superradiance. By choosing a certain coupling between the left and right boundaries, the two-point function is modified, and its first order correction contributes the negative energy to open the wormhole. The wormhole is most traversable when the perturbation is turned on at early times, with opening that depends on the mode's frequency, the black hole temperature, and the fermion mass. At late times, the average null energy has damped oscillation behavior until eventually reaches zero. Wormhole with lower temperature have less traversability and it is completely closed at extreme limit. The same traversability can also be reproduced by using eikonal method. On the other hand, rotation and the number of fields involved in the deformation can increases the upper bound on information transfer up to the order of the entropy. Additionally, symmetrical effective potential bumps connected by the wormhole can produce observable echoes. We find that the echo time delay cannot exceed the scrambling time of the black hole.

hep-th.title: A Monte Carlo Study of the Dipolar Universality Class in Three Dimensions
hep-th.author: Akira Matsumoto, Yu Nakayama, Toshiki Onagi, Slava Rychkov
hep-th.abstract: The dipolar universality class describes the phase transition in 3D ferromagnets with strong dipolar interactions, as first discussed by Aharony and Fisher in the 1970s. While this universality class has been studied theoretically using renormalization group methods, as well as experimentally, little is known about it from Monte Carlo simulations. In this paper, we aim to bridge this gap. We introduce a lattice model that faithfully implements the transverse constraint on the order parameter. We introduce a Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm which involves a combination of local Metropolis updates preserving the constraint, and a global update of the zero mode. We perform simulations on cubic lattices up to volume $48\times 48 \times 48$. We observe a continuous phase transition between the disordered and ordered phases. We obtain estimates of the critical exponent $\nu$ and the critical Binder ratio, and compare them with results from other techniques. We also study whether rotational invariance emerges at the critical point, and discuss the influence of the toroidal geometry on this question.

hep-th.title: A Dispersive Bootstrap for the Virasoro-Shapiro Amplitude
hep-th.author: Yongjun Xu
hep-th.abstract: We study the closed-string tree-level Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude using the dispersive S-matrix bootstrap. For the ten-dimensional maximally supersymmetric four-point amplitude, we impose analyticity, crossing symmetry, partial-wave unitarity, and Regge boundedness. With the massless graviton pole kept explicitly, the resulting dispersion relations and crossing null constraints give numerical bounds on the leading low-energy coefficients normalized by the gravitational coupling, which agree at our reference truncation with earlier bounds from smeared functionals. We then introduce a Virasoro-inspired ansatz, which becomes a set of nonlinear relations among Wilson coefficients and shrinks the allowed region toward the Virasoro-Shapiro trajectory. Finally, we study a gravity-pole-subtracted setup, where the regular part of the amplitude has a well-defined forward limit. In this stripped problem, on the slice of the leading coefficient that places the first Virasoro-Shapiro resonance at the cutoff, the nonlinear constraints reduce the allowed region to a small island containing the Virasoro-Shapiro point. Imposing the ansatz to all orders, together with spectral assumptions not used in the numerics, we show analytically that positivity selects the Virasoro-Shapiro spectrum.

hep-th.title: Holonomies and Boundary Symmetries in the Discrete BF Formulation of Carroll Dilaton Gravity
hep-th.author: H.T.Özer, Aytül Filiz
hep-th.abstract: We construct a discrete realization of two-dimensional Carroll dilaton gravity based on a BF-type gauge structure with holonomy variables on lattice links. The bulk theory remains topological, while the physical dynamics is encoded in boundary degrees of freedom. Imposing admissible boundary conditions, we derive the asymptotic symmetry structure directly at the lattice level. The least restrictive conditions yield an affine extension of the Carroll algebra, while additional constraints reduce the symmetry to a conformal sector governed by a discrete Virasoro-type algebra. In the continuum limit, the lattice symmetry structure reproduces the expected affine Carroll algebra together with its conformal reduction. The construction therefore provides the ultra-relativistic counterpart of discrete Jackiw-Teitelboim(JT) gravity.

hep-th.title: A UV-Finite Refinement of the Ryu-Takayanagi Relation in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$
hep-th.author: Philipp Dorau, Albert Much, Leonardo Sangaletti, Rainer Verch
hep-th.abstract: We establish a refined Ryu--Takayanagi (RT) relation in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ using \emph{relative entropy} as the central object, in place of the ultraviolet-divergent von Neumann entanglement entropy. Adapting Hollands' exact result for the chiral relative entropy to a diamond region, we express the boundary relative entropy between the vacuum and a coherent state as a Schwarzian functional, which the Fefferman--Graham dictionary identifies with the asymptotic data of a Bañados geometry; the rigidity of three-dimensional gravity promotes this boundary identification to the bulk. To linear order in the metric perturbation, the relative entropy then equals the variation of the RT geodesic length divided by $4G_N$. The construction rests only on the Bisognano--Wichmann/Borchers theorem and the holographic dictionary, giving a UV-finite, operator-algebraic counterpart to the RT relation.

hep-th.title: Morse Bridge between Planar Kepler and Hyperbolic Landau Dynamics
hep-th.author: Mikhail S. Plyushchay
hep-th.abstract: A common Morse Hamiltonian bridges the planar Kepler--Coulomb and hyperbolic Landau systems, linking flat electric dynamics to curved magnetic dynamics. A radial Liouville transformation with coupling-constant metamorphosis maps the separated Kepler problem to the Morse system, while fixed-horocyclic-momentum reduction maps the hyperbolic Landau problem to the same system. In a common normalization, the Coulomb coupling is the signed product of the magnetic field and conserved horocyclic momentum, while the quantum Landau reduction has the universal half-density shift $1/4$. Beyond this shared reduction, we construct a direct classical orbit map on the regular nonradial sectors for all signs of the Kepler energy. It maps the Landau height to a scaled inverse Kepler radius, Kepler ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas to magnetic circles, horocycles and hypercycles, and Hamilton's hodograph affinely to the Landau carrier circle. The reduced Kepler symplectic form and the Binet-selected complex structure determine a Poincaré Kähler metric. Its nondegenerate Binet orbits have constant geodesic curvature of magnitude equal to the inverse eccentricity, while zero coupling gives geodesics. The orbit map identifies this metric isometrically with the Poincaré configuration-space metric of the hyperbolic Landau problem. Composing the quantum Liouville maps eliminates the Morse wavefunction and yields an exact weighted intertwining identity between the radial Kepler and horocyclic Landau operator pencils. At distinguished half-integer magnetic fields, the angular-momentum grading of a fixed Kepler shell is reorganized into the finite reduced Landau tower and its threshold endpoint. These exact correspondences hold in the stated reduced sectors despite the unitary inequivalence of the complete parent systems.

hep-th.title: Combinatorial aspects of holographic quantum secret sharing
hep-th.author: Ning Bao, Keiichiro Furuya, Jacob March
hep-th.abstract: We introduce combinatorial holographic quantum secret sharing (CHQSS) for a bulk subregion in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ to study how logical information of the bulk subregion is encoded in the boundary and protected from erasures of boundary subregions. We introduce a distance, a reconstruction threshold, and a secret threshold to characterize CHQSS schemes. We present the phase transitions of multipartite entanglement wedges in a symmetric setup and observe multiple distinct phase transition points. The distance and thresholds depend on the holographic phase and the choice of bulk subregion. We derive the maximum distance. Moreover, we derive the relations between the distance and the thresholds. We construct a family of CHQSS schemes in the symmetric setting that includes perfect threshold CHQSS and perfect non-threshold CHQSS.

hep-th.title: Fortuity and fragility in supersymmetric SYK
hep-th.author: James Chryssanthacopoulos, David Vegh
hep-th.abstract: In the $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetric SYK model with $N$ fermions, every BPS state is fortuitous: at fixed charge, it exists only over a finite range of $N$. Allowing the charge to increase, we show that BPS classes may instead be uplifted along lattice walks inside the fortuity window, potentially to arbitrarily large $N$. However, there is no canonical uplift. We therefore introduce a decoder $D$ whose spectrum quantifies exact uplift and its metric cost. We call the failure or increasing cost of uplifting harmonic representatives metric fragility. Chen's single-matrix model and the protected tower of the two-flavor SYK model realize bare and genuinely dressed mechanisms of perfect uplift, respectively. In the generic one-flavor model, exact uplift eventually fails. The Lin-Maldacena-Rozenberg-Shan-type operator $D^\dagger D$ exhibits level statistics consistent with the Gaussian unitary ensemble. Its eigenvalues quantify the metric continuity of BPS states across system size, while their correlations probe chaos within the BPS sector. Metric fragility and BPS chaos are thus encoded in complementary observables of the same operator, distinguishing chaotic BPS sectors from exactly solvable towers.

hep-th.title: Universal Emergence of Bosonic and Fermionic Algebras in a Deterministic Proper-Time Framework
hep-th.author: Alessio Maiezza
hep-th.abstract: This work develops the deterministic, discrete proper-time framework introduced in our previous work, Eur.\ Phys.\ J.\ C \textbf{86} (2026) 829, in which quantum field theory emerges as an effective infrared description characterized by a running Planck constant. There, the effective quantization scale was inferred from the microscopic multiplicity unresolved by coarse-graining. Here, we provide its dynamical and operatorial realization and extend the construction to fermionic degrees of freedom. First, consistency under changes of macroscopic resolution leads to the structure of the Renormalization Group Equation, while the running Planck constant governs the crossover toward the deterministic regime. Second, we represent the reversible microscopic dynamics through finite-difference translations in field-configuration space. After coarse-graining, the resulting operator-valued canonical commutation relations reproduce the same quantization scale previously obtained from statistical microstate counting, thereby linking microscopic evolution to the emergent canonical algebra. Third, representing the same update within a Grassmann algebra yields the corresponding canonical anticommutation relations. The bosonic and fermionic sectors thus inherit a common effective Planck constant without introducing an independent fermionic update or quantization scale. Finally, we discuss possible implications for high-energy loop amplitudes and effective Hawking radiation.

hep-th.title: Bogomol'nyi equations for Kruglov strings
hep-th.author: I. Prasetyo, U. Ubaydillah, H. S. Ramadhan
hep-th.abstract: We construct the Bogomol'nyi equations for Abelian gauge--Higgs vortices in which the Maxwell gauge sector is replaced by Kruglov nonlinear electrodynamics, a power-law family that interpolates between Maxwell theory, Born--Infeld electrodynamics, and exponential electrodynamics, characterized by a dimensionless exponent $\sigma$. Using the stressless method, we derive a pair of first-order equations directly from the vanishing of the spatial stress tensor, without assuming the Higgs potential \textit{a priori}. For generic $\sigma$, the gauge and Higgs sectors are coupled through an implicit algebraic relation. We therefore introduce a constitutive map $\Phi(Y;\sigma)$ and analyze its monotonicity and range to determine the conditions for a smooth admissible Bogomol'nyi branch. For $\sigma>1/2$, the constitutive map is strictly monotonic and unbounded, whereas for $0<\sigma<1/2$ it possesses a finite maximum; the marginal case $\sigma=1/2$ is bounded. These properties yield explicit bounds on the nonlinear parameter $\beta$ for the latter cases. We further obtain closed-form constitutive relations, BPS potentials, and gauge-field equations for six representative values of $\sigma$, spanning linear, quadratic, and cubic algebraic structures. The corresponding vortex profiles are then computed numerically. The resulting BPS string tension is purely topological, $\mu_{\rm BPS}=2\pi n$, independent of both $\sigma$ and $\beta$.

hep-th.title: Thermodynamics of Lorentzian Taub-NUT spacetimes in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet AdS gravity
hep-th.author: Borja Diez
hep-th.abstract: We study the thermodynamics of Lorentzian Taub-NUT spacetimes in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet AdS gravity in arbitrary even dimensions, constructed as $U(1)$ fibrations over Einstein-Kähler base manifolds. We compute the temperature from the surface gravity and the energy as the conserved charge associated with the stationary Killing vector using the off-shell Abbott-Deser-Tekin formalism. Within the same framework, we obtain the entropy as a horizon Noether charge. The result agrees with the Iyer-Wald formula and includes a Gauss-Bonnet correction to the Bekenstein-Hawking area law. Retaining the Misner strings whenever present, we formulate a first law of full cohomogeneity in which the NUT parameter varies independently of the horizon radius. This requires an additional NUT-related thermodynamic variable and its conjugate potential, which we determine explicitly. We also briefly discuss the static limit.

hep-th.title: BRST quantization of the induced gauge theory for the Higgs-branch CFT${}_2$
hep-th.author: Bogdan Stefański Jr
hep-th.abstract: We study Witten's induced gauge theory associated with the D1-D5 Higgs-branch CFT${}_2$, in which the non-dynamical vector multiplet becomes reanimated by integrating out the fundamental hypermultiplets. We propose a BRST quantisation of this theory and derive its induced propagators. We show that the ghost sector first contributes at subleading order, that the induced $A\phi^2$ vertex satisfies the Slavnov-Taylor identity and that gauge-invariant correlators are independent of the gauge parameter. Together with our chosen regularization prescription, this gives a perturbative framework for computing observables in the induced theory.

hep-th.title: A gravitational realization of Courant--Hilbert deformations
hep-th.author: Osamu Fukushima, Miyabi Kurihara, Takaki Matsumoto, Kentaroh Yoshida
hep-th.abstract: Courant--Hilbert (CH) deformations unify broad classes of solvable stress-tensor flows including $T\bar{T}$ and root-$T\bar{T}$. However, a gravitational action that systematically yields such general deformations has remained unknown. In this Letter, we construct a two-dimensional massive gravity theory whose on-shell action reproduces the complete CH deformation. The gravity sector is defined via an arbitrary function of the eigenvalue ratio $y$ of the relative zweibein. To bypass the technical difficulty of directly eliminating the auxiliary zweibein, we reformulate the matter sector using a $2 \times 2$ spectral decomposition involving $y$ and a rank-one projector $K$. Sequentially solving the equations of motion---first for $K$ and subsequently for $y$---naturally maps the system onto the Russo-Townsend form of the CH flow. Our work extends Tolley's massive gravity formulation of $T\bar{T}$ flows to the CH landscape, providing a clear geometric mechanism for solvable stress-tensor flows.

hep-th.title: Extremal black hole mimickers: geometry, stability, and long-delay signal trains
hep-th.author: Sergey N. Solodukhin
hep-th.abstract: We present a spacetime that serves as a horizonless mimicker of extremal black holes. Unlike previously studied mimickers of black holes with non-degenerate horizons, whose geometries are of the wormhole type and consist of two asymptotically flat regions connected by a very long throat, the mimicker of an extremal black hole possesses a single asymptotically flat region at one end and an infinitely long throat at the other. In the throat region, the spacetime approaches the direct-product geometry $M_{1,1} \times S^2$, where $M_{1,1}$ is two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime and $S^2$ is the two-sphere. We investigate scalar-field dynamics and the fate of the Aretakis instability. Although Aretakis-like modes arise in a local analysis of the throat, they do not lead to a physical instability of the mimicker. A scalar perturbation initially localized in the throat gives rise, at late times, to a sequence of signals with a characteristic separation $t_{\rm delay}\sim 1/\lambda$, where $\lambda\ll 1$ is a deformation parameter. This timescale is parametrically larger than the echo time $t_{\rm echo}\sim \ln(1/\lambda)$ characteristic of non-extremal black-hole mimickers. We refer to this sequence as a {\it long-delay signal train}. Geometrically, the periodicity of the long-delay signals is associated with periodic geodesics on $S^2$. We then extend the construction to extremal Kerr. In this case, the throat region approaches a generalized product geometry involving $M_{1,1}$ and a two-dimensional surface $\Sigma_2$. The corresponding signals are expected to form a quasi-periodic signal train, reflecting the quasi-periodic geodesic motion on $\Sigma_2$. We also comment on the generalization to wormhole mimickers of non-extremal black holes and on the implications of these results for unitarity in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence.

hep-th.title: Krylov complexity and oscillatory quantum dynamics in two-field inflation
hep-th.author: Tao Li, Lei-Hua Liu, Hai-Bing Fu
hep-th.abstract: We investigate Krylov-space dynamics of primordial perturbations in two-field inflation. Starting from the quadratic action for coupled curvature and entropy perturbations, we solve the mode equations with Bunch-Davies initial conditions and construct the corresponding quadratic Hamiltonian. The Gaussian quantum state is described by a four-mode squeezed state with two squeezing channels. We derive the evolution of the squeezing strength and squeezing angle and use them to evaluate the Krylov complexity, Krylov entropy, and channel-resolved Lanczos coefficients. Our numerical results show that the two channels remain weakly squeezed inside the horizon but develop different squeezing histories after horizon exit. The second channel develops strong squeezing earlier and dominates the intermediate evolution, whereas the first channel shows a delayed enhancement. The corresponding Krylov complexities exhibit distinct oscillatory structures across horizon crossing and pronounced fluctuations in the strongly squeezed superhorizon regime. The corresponding Krylov complexities exhibit distinct oscillatory structures across horizon crossing and pronounced fluctuations in the strongly squeezed superhorizon regime. These features arise from the phase-sensitive squeezing dynamics and reflect the different responses of the two channels to curvature-entropy coupling.

hep-th.title: Reference frame dependence of the periodically oscillating Coulomb field in the Proca theory
hep-th.author: Bogdan Damski
hep-th.abstract: The Proca theory of the real massive vector field admits non-equilibrium solutions, where the asymptotic dynamics of its electric field is dominated by the periodically oscillating Coulomb component. We discuss how such field configurations are seen in different reference frames, where we find an intriguing spatial pattern of the vector field of the Proca theory and the electromagnetic field associated with it.

hep-th.title: Chaotic Imprints in Gravitational Waves from Extreme-Mass-Ratio-Inspirals Embedded in Dark Matter Halo
hep-th.author: Surajit Das, Surojit Dalui, Bum-Hoon Lee, Yi-Fu Cai
hep-th.abstract: We investigate imprints of chaos in gravitational waves from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals configuration, where a stellar massive object, confined in an external potential as a harmonic oscillators, orbits a supermassive Schwarzschild-like black hole embedded in a Dehnen-type dark matter halo. In our previous work (Das S, et al., Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals embedded in dark matter halo: Existence of homoclinic orbit and horizon-induced chaos, Sci. China-Phys. Mech. Astron. 69, 290413 (2026)), we demonstrated the system's transition from non-chaotic to chaotic dynamics by analyzing Poincaré sections, orbital evolution, and Lyapunov exponents across different energies and dark matter halo parameters. In this work, we compute the gravitational waveforms of the small celestial object along different chaotic and non-chaotic orbits by implementing the numerical kludge scheme. We further perform spectral analysis of the gravitational waveforms from such orbits. In particular, we show that when the system is in a chaotic state, the gravitational wave signals are characterized by broader frequency spectra with finite widths, irregular waveform modulations with comparatively large strain excursions for the chaotic trajectories considered here, together with modified energy-emission characteristics, distinctly differentiating them from the signals generated during the system's non-chaotic state.
