Furthermore, we discuss the potential detectability of these orbits for upcoming observatories like Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA), TianQin, and Taiji, emphasizing the significant potential for detecting chaotic imprints in gravitational waves to substantially enhance our understanding of chaotic dynamics in black hole physics and the dark matter environments of galactic nuclei.

hep-th.title: Self-resonance preheating in deformed attractor models: oscillon formation and evolution
hep-th.author: Bao-Min Gu, Yu-Peng Zhang, Fu-Wen Shu, Yu-Xiao Liu
hep-th.abstract: It is well known that, in potentials that are quadratic near the minimum but shallower away, such as small-$\alpha$ ($\alpha \ll M_P^2$) attractors, the inflaton condensate fragments into localized compact objects known as oscillons during self-resonance preheating. In this work, we investigate self-resonance in a deformed $\alpha$-attractor T-model with a Gaussian feature near the minimum, distant from the end of inflation. Linear analysis reveals altered resonance bands and deformed Floquet charts dependent on feature parameters, primarily through the localized modification of $V''(\phi)$. In fully nonlinear lattice simulations, we find that the potential feature has only a modest influence on gradient-energy transfer during resonance, whereas the subsequent evolution becomes strongly dependent on the Gaussian feature's dimensionless amplitude $h$. Increasing $|h|$ suppresses the formation and persistence of compact oscillons, resulting in fewer objects and a smaller fraction of energy stored in them. The total-energy and internal-gradient-energy diagnostics give consistent lifetime trends. Within the directly resolved range, the oscillon lifetime decreases nonlinearly with increasing $|h|$, with negative $h$ generally producing shorter lifetimes than positive $h$ of the same magnitude. The gravitational wave emission is dominated by the resonant stage and becomes strongly suppressed after oscillon formation. We further find an enhancement in the high-frequency tail of the spectrum, sourced by the potential feature. Although a complete reheating description requires external couplings and higher-resolution simulations, clear qualitative differences in the post-inflationary expansion history already emerge within our simulated time window. These results clarify how potential features affect preheating dynamics and oscillon evolution.

hep-th.title: Thermodynamic Gravity with Non-Extensive Horizon Entropy and Topological Calibration
hep-th.author: Marco Figliolia, Petr Jizba, Gaetano Lambiase
hep-th.abstract: We revisit Jacobson's thermodynamic derivation of gravity for generalized, non-extensive horizon entropies and develop a consistent framework in which modified gravitational dynamics emerge from horizon thermodynamics. By interpreting $S(A)$ as a coarse-grained entropy entering the thermodynamic constitutive relation, we show that only its local slope at a reference area $A_*$ contributes to macroscopic dynamics within a local Rindler-wedge construction. In this setting, the Clausius relation is reformulated as a stationarity condition for a Massieu functional at fixed Unruh temperature, allowing the entropy slope $s_0=(dS/dA)|_{A_*}$ to be identified as the parameter controlling the effective gravitational coupling. For entropy linear in area, Einstein's equations are recovered with $G_{\mathrm{eff}}=1/(4s_0)$. As a separate consistency check, we demonstrate that a scalar-response extension of the horizon entropy density, supplemented by internal entropy production, correctly reproduces the field equations of $f(R)$ gravity. Motivated by group-entropic arguments and generalized thermodynamics, we adopt a power-law entropy $S(A)=\eta(A/4G)^{\delta}$ and study its implications across scales. To remove the ambiguity in the coarse-graining scale, we introduce a Topological Calibration Principle linking the reference area to intrinsic geometric data through the Gauss-Bonnet theorem. For compact cross-sections admitted by the chosen theory or boundary conditions, this yields a topology-dependent effective coupling governed by the Euler characteristic. Consistency requirements constrain deviations from extensivity and generate scale-dependent modifications with potentially observable cosmological signatures. The resulting framework provides a systematic setting for testing non-extensive horizon thermodynamics and its phenomenological implications.

hep-th.title: Universality classes, Thermodynamics of Group Entropies, and Black Holes
hep-th.author: Henrik Jeldtoft Jensen, Petr Jizba, Piergiulio Tempesta
hep-th.abstract: Conventional Boltzmann--Gibbs statistical mechanics successfully describes systems with weak to moderate correlations, in which the number of accessible configurations $W(N)$ grows exponentially with the number of degrees of freedom $N$. However, this framework breaks down for systems for which the effectively occupied configuration space exhibits non-exponential growth. While numerous generalized entropies have been proposed to address this limitation, a coherent link to classical thermodynamic laws has remained elusive. Here, we propose group entropies as a unifying framework, defining universality classes of entropies through the asymptotic scaling of $W(N)$, each yielding an extensive entropy. We show that this approach provides the basis for a consistent thermodynamic formulation beyond the Boltzmann--Gibbs paradigm. In particular, by expressing these entropies in terms of thermodynamic state variables, we demonstrate their consistency with classical thermodynamics, in close analogy to the emergence of the Clausius entropy from the Boltzmann--Gibbs formalism. Focusing on the zeroth thermodynamic law, we identify the empirical temperature and, by using Carathéodory's formulation of the second law, we derive the associated absolute temperature. As an application, we analyse black-hole thermodynamics using the extensive group entropy class corresponding to stretched-exponential behaviour of $W(N)$ and derive a negative heat capacity, known to be a hallmark property of black holes. This result holds for the stretched-exponential entropies associated with both the Bekenstein--Hawking and Barrow entropy scalings.

hep-th.title: Analytic formulae for non-local nonstabiliserness in bipartite systems of qutrits and ququints
hep-th.author: Giorgio Busoni, John Gargalionis, Ewan N. V. Wallace, Martin J. White
hep-th.abstract: We conjecture analytic expressions for the non-local magic of bipartite pure qudit states of prime local dimension. Our construction relies on the Schmidt-aligned state attaining the minimum over local unitaries, a hypothesis that we support with numerical evidence for pairs of qutrits and ququints. For composite local dimensions, we find that the analogous expressions do not in general reproduce the global minimum, but can still provide computationally cheap approximations to the non-local magic. We also find that relations between non-local magic and entanglement diagnostics that hold for two qubits generally do not extend to qutrit and higher-dimensional systems. As a few-body application, we evaluate the qutrit non-local magic generated by elastic pion scattering, treating hadronic isospin as the qutrit. We find that $p$-wave charged pion scattering realises the maximum non-local magic allowed in the system just below the $\rho$-meson resonance.

hep-th.title: Revisiting Constraints on Primordial Curvature Power Spectrum from PBH Abundances
hep-th.author: Ashu Kushwaha, Teruaki Suyama
hep-th.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) can form in the early Universe, during radiation domination, from the collapse of large-amplitude density perturbations shortly after horizon re-entry. This mechanism establishes an approximate one-to-one correspondence between the PBH mass and the scale of the peak in the primordial curvature perturbations. Consequently, the constraints on PBH abundances can be translated into upper limits on the amplitude of the primordial curvature power spectrum, providing an indirect probe of the last e-folds of inflation corresponding to these smaller scales. We derive constraints on the amplitude of primordial curvature power spectra with both narrow and broad peaks using up-to-date bounds on PBH abundances. Given the theoretical uncertainties in PBH formation, we systematically compare the constraints obtained using the Press-Schechter (PS) formalism and peak theory, accounting for the nonlinear relation between curvature perturbations and density contrast, and assess the impact of different window functions and the transfer function. We quantify the impact of spherical versus nonspherical collapse criteria and show that including non-sphericity significantly increases the inferred amplitude of the primordial power spectrum, reflecting the larger threshold density contrast required for PBH formation. We also find that whereas the constraints obtained using the PS formalism and peak theory remain largely similar for the monochromatic case, they differ in the case of a broad primordial power spectrum. This discrepancy underscores that current constraints remain sensitive to the choice of statistical formalism. Our consistent treatment of monochromatic and extended mass functions provides a systematic mapping based on existing methodologies, while highlighting that reducing these theoretical uncertainties is a crucial step toward probing the early Universe through PBHs.

hep-th.title: Separability from Multipartite Measures
hep-th.author: Chen-Te Ma, Ma-Ke Yuan
hep-th.abstract: We show that multi-invariants provide necessary and sufficient criteria for full separability in finite-dimensional multipartite systems. For tripartite three-qubit states, the third-order negativity gives an exact criterion for full separability for both pure and mixed states. We then extend the framework to four-qubit pure states, whose full characterization requires eighteen independent real parameters. We identify eighteen independent entanglement measures, consisting of six bipartite, eight tripartite, and four quadripartite measures, with the third-order negativity serving as a key separability criterion. Finally, we generalize the construction to multipartite qudit systems and discuss an application to conformal field theory.

hep-th.title: Vacuum stability in Geometric Trinity of Gravity
hep-th.author: Vincenzo Branchina, Salvatore Capozziello, Filippo Contino, Carmen Ferrara
hep-th.abstract: We investigate whether the classical equivalence of general relativity, its teleparallel equivalent, and its symmetric teleparallel equivalent extends to false-vacuum decay at leading semiclassical order. For a real scalar field minimally coupled to gravity, we compare the tunnelling exponent $B=S_{\rm b}-S_{\rm fv}$, which determines the exponential suppression of the decay rate, $\Gamma\sim e^{-B}$, with the Euclidean bounce, $S_{\rm b}$, and false-vacuum actions, $S_{\rm fv}$. The three formulations admit the same $O(4)$-symmetric Coleman-De Luccia bounce, but the boundary terms relating their actions can contribute to $B$. We explicitly evaluate the torsion and non-metricity boundary contributions at the regular origin, $r=0$, and at the asymptotic endpoint, $r\to\infty$. For regular configurations with consistently matched bounce and false-vacuum boundary data, these contributions vanish in both TEGR and STEGR. We therefore obtain $B_{\rm GR}=B_{\rm TEGR}=B_{\rm STEGR}$, establishing that the three formulations predict the same leading semiclassical suppression of false-vacuum decay within the class of configurations and boundary conditions considered.

hep-th.title: Time-dependent integrable quantum field theories with dynamical boundaries
hep-th.author: Pradip Kattel
hep-th.abstract: We present a general method to construct and solve time-dependent integrable chiral quantum field theories on finite intervals from autonomous scattering and reflection data. Spatial homogeneity forces the spectral labels of right- and left-moving particles to be affine with a common slope, so bulk and boundary couplings sample one spectral trajectory. A complete round trip shifts the spectral labels and gives boundary quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equations. The Yang--Baxter and reflection equations provide local consistency, while boundary-qKZ flatness provides global consistency. We reconstruct the local Hamiltonian by Cayley inversion of the bulk and boundary matching matrices. We apply the construction to rational $SU(N)$ scattering with fundamental boundary impurities and to an $O(3)$ model with a spin-$\tfrac12$ impurity. For the $SU(2)$ impurity, we construct explicit boundary-qKZ solutions as lattice sums of off-shell boundary Bethe vectors and recover the static open-chain Bethe equations when the drive rate vanishes

hep-th.title: Resistive alignment of a black-hole magnetosphere
hep-th.author: Ruben Lier, Oliver Porth
hep-th.abstract: Recent numerical simulations have shown that black-hole magnetospheres evolve rapidly toward alignment between the magnetic axis and spin axis but the physical origin of this process has remained unclear. We develop an analytic theory of this alignment within resistive relativistic magnetohydrodynamics. Taking the slow-spin Blandford-Znajek monopole solution as the exterior magnetic field, we reduce the induction equation to a relaxation equation for the current-sheet inclination angle. Our analysis shows that alignment results from second-order spin effects in the Blandford-Znajek solution combined with explicit resistive dissipation. We test this prediction using resistive-GRMHD simulations at several spins and resistivities and compare the measured late-time secular decay with the analytic prediction. This alignment timescale hence carries a unique signature which combines plasma dissipation with spacetime rotation.
